articles.title: Hearts 2-3 Monaco: Wouter Vrancken proud of players despite last-gasp Conference League defeat
articles.summary: Hearts lost 3-2 at home to Monaco in the Conference League; Jordi Altena opened the scoring; Sabah Kerjota pulled the Jambos back level after goals from Folarin Balogun and Edan Diop; Balogun netted again in stoppage-time; the Jambos have one point from their opening four games
articles.body:
The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.

But in the fourth and final minute of added time, injury-hit Hearts were denied what would have been a hugely commendable result when USA forward Balogun found space in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco's perfect record in the competition.

"The biggest thing is, of course, to be really proud of the performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side," said Vrancken, keen to reiterate that his team remains without several key players.

"Knowing that we have still nine injuries, I will mention it, and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and to still do this against that team, I'm really proud of what we did."

A point would have significantly boosted Hearts' hopes of reaching the knockout phase, but they can now only finish on a maximum of seven points - the same tally they managed two years ago before being eliminated on goal difference under Neil Critchley.

With their goal difference currently standing at minus five, Hearts will likely need high-scoring victories against Bosnian side Borac and Cypriot outfit Pafos in their final two matches to stand a chance of breaking into the top 24 and extending their European campaign beyond Christmas.

Vrancken, however, does not believe the late goal will make a significant difference to his side's prospects.

"I think the point doesn't make a difference," he said. "One or no points doesn't change anything in the next games. There's also something that really was pleasing for me, that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go.

"We wanted to go for the win here, and against a side like this, in the situation we're in, so really proud of this also, because three points would make a difference.

"Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games." Vrancken believes the quality of the goals scored by Altena and Kerjota, both exquisite finishes from range, highlighted the renewed belief coursing through his squad after their 8-0 win over Dundee last weekend.

"They were quality goals," he said. "You see the confidence those guys have, and this is what we wanted after the weekend, of course, that you take some confidence of the dynamics we did there.

"I think the conviction around the box was there, also in both boxes actually. It's an important thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games."

articles.title: Matarazzo: "Jon Martín y Mateta están forcejeando, pero los árbitros también tienen días buenos y malos..."
articles.standfirst: El técnico de la Real lamentó un día más las muchas ocasiones erradas por su equipo
articles.summary: El técnico de la Real lamentó un día más las muchas ocasiones erradas por su equipo
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo consideró como clave en la derrota de su Real Sociedad la acción del penalti y segunda amarilla de Jon Martín señalada por el árbitro, que a su juicio tuvo una actuación irregular. El técnico de Nueva Jersey ve ya imposible el top 8 y quiere, al menos, conseguir clasificarse entre los 24 equipos que sigan en la competición. Matarazzo analizó así la derrota final de su equipo ante el Crystal Palace. “Ha sido un muy buen partido nuestro hasta el penalti, concedido en un saque de banda y que ha cambiado el partido. Hemos sido el mejor equipo, controlando el juego, intentando que no nos atacasen mucho y haciéndolo nosotros, con ocasiones para hacer más goles que el que hicimos, y hemos merecido ganar, pero no lo hemos conseguido”. ¿Cómo vio la acción del penalti? “Creo que Mateta también estaba tirando de Jon Martín, que ambos están forcejeando. La doble tarjeta amarilla o la roja en el penalti fue una acción decisiva en este encuentro. El árbitro ha tenido un partido un poco raro, no ha sido muy consistente para mí, hemos visto como pitaba, la primera amarilla de Jon Martín no ha sido, pero los árbitros tienen buenos días y malos, como los jugadores”. Matarazzo lamentó que su Real haya enlazado dos derrotas, la de Santander y la del Crystal Palace, sin merecerlas. “El fútbol es como la vida, no siempre tienes lo que mereces, pero tienes que seguir insistiendo, trabajando, creando tu propia suerte. El top 8 no podrá ser, pero la clasificación sí y seguiremos intentando llegar lo más lejos posible en esta competición”.

articles.title: Georgian police clash with Turkiye’s Besiktas fans over Palestinian flag
articles.summary: Match between Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva suspended for 30 minutes after confrontation between fans and police.
articles.body:
Georgian police have clashed with fans of Turkiye’s Besiktas after they unfurled a Palestinian flag during a Europa League game against Israel’s Hapoel Beer-Sheva.

The clashes resulted in a suspension of about 30 minutes during the 26th minute of the game held in Batumi, Georgia, but it resumed after the interruption on Thursday. Besiktas eventually won 2-1.

Turkish media outlets reported that Georgian police entered the stands and used pepper spray against fans of the Istanbul giant, prompting Danish referee Morten Krogh to stop the game with the score 0-0.

The game was relocated by UEFA to Batumi after Turkish authorities said Istanbul could not host it for safety and security reasons. Unlike two previous Hapoel away games, spectators were allowed in the stadium.

Besiktas accused Georgian police of using “disproportionate” force against supporters before and during the game.

“We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans,” the Turkish club said in a statement. “We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents.”

The Turkish Football Federation also strongly condemned the treatment of Besiktas supporters, saying they were subjected to unacceptable behaviour and discrimination in a statement on X. The federation said it would press for an investigation into the incident.

Several other Turkish Super Lig clubs, including Trabzonspor, Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, Erzurumspor, Basaksehir and Samsunspor, condemned the use of force against Besiktas fans.

Prior to the match, Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu Agency reported.

A video published by Besiktas on X after the game shows their players posing for a picture behind fans carrying a banner that reads: “Rise up against the occupation. Freedom for Palestine.”

Turkish Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci spoke to his Georgian counterpart following the game to discuss Turkiye’s concern over the incident.

According to Turkiye’s Interior Ministry, Ciftci expressed concern over the disproportionate use of force against Turkish fans and called for measures to ensure their safe return to Turkiye.

Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili reportedly said that UEFA officials had confiscated the fans’ Palestinian flags and that Georgian state authorities had played no role in the confiscation.

articles.summary: El delantero del Racing suma 11 goles en 13 partidos
articles.body: Levante y Racing llevan dinámicas opuestas. Mientra los valencianos llevan cuatro partidos ligueros seguidos sin ganar, los cántabros suman dos victorias consecutivas y están a dos puntos de los puestos europeos. Zabiri, con 11 goles en 13 partidos, es la gran amenaza para los granotas, que luchan por alejarse del descenso. El Levante, en decimoquinta posición, empatado a puntos con el descenso, intentará despegarse de la zona roja si consigue un nuevo triunfo un mes después. Para este envite, Luís Castro tendrá las bajas de Manu Sánchez, por una rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla izquierda; y Jeremy Toljan, tras una lesión de grado moderado en la musculatura isquiotibial de la pierna derecha. También está la duda de Petar Ratkov que no ha estado presente en el entrenamiento de este jueves por molestias musculares. El Racing viaja a Valencia para enfrentarse al Levante después de sumar dos victorias consecutivas ante Málaga y Real Sociedad y ubicarse en el séptimo puesto de la tabla. José Alberto cuenta para este choque con las bajas de Mantilla, Andrés Martín y Maguette, por lesión. Todo parece indicar que el técnico asturiano repetirá el mismo once que venció a la Real Sociedad en El Sardinero. Quizá la única duda está en la banda derecha entre Iker Luque y Pablo García. articles.title: Hearts' European hopes hang by a thread but Vrancken proud
articles.summary: Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken expresses both pride and disappointment after his team came out on the wrong side of a five-goal thriller against Monaco.
articles.body:
There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.

Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.

Now they have little to no margin for error in their two remaining league phase matches.

They will likely have to beat both Borac Banja Luka of Bosnia and Cyprus' Pafos to reach the knockout stages, but if they perform as they did against Monaco, they will give themselves a fighting chance.

Hearts have garnered a reputation as entertainers under Vrancken - scoring a raft of goals while being porous at the back.

This game was their season in microcosm. The goals - scored by Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota - were things of beauty, picture-perfect strikes worthy of any stage.

But as thrilling as Hearts were in attack, they were as baffling at the back.

Jamie McCart unnecessarily tripped Matthis Abline, allowing Balogun to score from the penalty spot and Monaco's second came from Altena giving the ball away.

"It's Gladiators - are we not entertained? It's sensational," said Hearts legend John Robertson at half-time, with the game finely poised at 2-2.

Monaco strike in 94th minute to break Hearts in five-goal epic

Latest Hearts news, analysis and fan views

Both teams had chances to win it in the second half, but it was Monaco who took theirs in the final stages. Mamadou Coulibaly was afforded too much space and he slipped Balogun through to beat Beau Reus.

"It's a lack of nous and a little bit of naivety," former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart said on TNT Sports. "McCart backs off and allows the ball to be played into Balogun's feet."

Despite the frustrating nature of the late concession, Vrancken's overwhelming emotion was of pride.

"I'm very disappointed with how we give the goal away at the end," he said.

"The biggest thing is the pride for the performance today. Against a side of Monaco's [quality] - we're still missing nine players through injury - this performance was really pleasing."

Before the recent international break, Hearts were beaten 3-1 by Swiss outfit Thun, before a shock 5-2 home defeat by high-flying Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership.

However, they bounced back with a ruthless 8-0 win at Dundee on Saturday and carried that confidence into this game against a team with a far bigger budget.

"You saw that the confidence was there from the weekend and there was conviction around their box," Vrancken added. "It will not work every time, but the conviction and energy was there again.

"Our team kept their heads in the game and kept going for it, not being pleased with 2-2. Really pleased with what I saw."

Aside from his dismay at Balogun's winner and how it came about, Vrancken's main gripe was with the officials.

He felt there was a foul on Kerjota in the build-up to Monaco's second goal and was bemused at the fact neither Takumi Minamino and Denis Zakaria were sent off.

Minamino - already on a yellow card - wiped out Sabri Guendouz on the edge of the Monaco box, but got away with a warning. And VAR opted not to intervene after Zakaria went over the top of the ball and caught Pierre Landry Kabore on the shin.

"The second goal, they pulled Sabah [Kerjota] and he can't do his defensive work," Vrancken said.

"It was not the only refereeing decision that was interesting tonight. I don't know how it's possible not to give a red card for the tackle on [Pierre Landry Kabore]. It's clearly above the ankle, so it's always a red card.

"And why didn't Minamino get a second yellow before half-time? He prevents a shot from Sabri at the edge of the box.

"The explanation of the fourth official was even more crazy - he explained it could be for his first yellow card, but not for his second yellow. It was clearly a yellow card and then we were against 10 in the second half."

articles.title: 'Priceless' Duran proves 'the man' but is he papering over cracks at Celtic?
articles.summary: Camilo Duran's 15-goal haul this season has made him an invaluable player for a Celtic side fighting for European progression.
articles.body:
"Duran is priceless for us at the moment".

It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran.

With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side.

His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive.

Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team currently 13th in the Portuguese second tier.

Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play.

"He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," said O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas.

"Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something.

"He's not a big guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer."

Papering over cracks or quality in depth?

Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh.

While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh , the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart.

Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice.

"I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden said on Sportsound post-match.

Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable.

Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park.

If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real plan of attack.

Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus.

Arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form.

Duran spares Celtic's blushes against Portuguese second-tier side Torreense

Brian: Embarrassed by that performance, I know that there no easy games in Europe, couldn't pass the ball, not fit enough, no style of play and poorly coached. The club is in decline.

John: Celtic are just an average side these days - there should be no expectation.

Ted: That was just embarrassing. The 31st team in Portugal made us look ordinary. Go now Martin with dignity intact and preserve your achievements. Thus mob will drag you down.

Allan: Outclassed and out paced by Torreense, Celtic played poorly with a lot of comedy of errors in their play. But Yippee hee, Celtic. Won with a late goal from Duran.

Liam: This can't go on any further now, regardless of the result. MON is done and the coaching staff are done. Booing substitutions is the end, never mind a performance like this against second division opposition. The board can resign too.

Alec: Total embarrassment. Barring Jota, there was a complete lack of creativity, quality, urgency and belief. Time for the board to make the right decisions, get a new manager in and get rid of at least 10 of those players on show tonight.

articles.title: Un árbitro le pega un sangriento puñetazo al portero que le mentó a su madre: "No me noqueó"
articles.standfirst: El portero Christian Martínez declaró que el golpe del árbitro Jordy Alemán le hizo sangrar la boca, pero que no logró "noquearlo"
articles.summary: El portero Christian Martínez declaró que el golpe del árbitro Jordy Alemán le hizo sangrar la boca, pero que no logró "noquearlo"
articles.body: El árbitro boliviano Jordy Alemán está en medio de una polémica por el puñetazo que propinó al arquero argentino Christian Martínez, del Real Potosí, durante el partido de vuelta de la final de la Copa Bolivia, el segundo torneo más importante del país andino, contra el Always Ready. El partido, disputado en el estadio Víctor Agustín Ugarte, en Potosí, acabó con el marcador sin goles, aunque el Always Ready se coronó campeón porque llevaba la ventaja del 3-1 logrado en la ida en su bastión en la ciudad de El Alto, a más de 4.100 metros de altitud. La gresca ocurrió cuando Jordy Alemán dictaminó el final del partido, tras lo cual un grupo de jugadores de la escuadra lila rodeó al árbitro para reprocharle sus decisiones durante el encuentro. Alemán, quien en ese momento estaba sin resguardo policial, respondió con un golpe de puño en el rostro del portero. En medio de la riña, el juez expulsó a cuatro jugadores y tres integrantes del cuerpo técnico potosino. Después del incidente, aún alterado, Martínez declaró que el golpe del árbitro le hizo sangrar la boca, pero que no logró "noquearlo". También admitió haberle dicho "que se le muera la mamá", además de pedir que le "vuelva" todo el "mal" que, según dijo, hizo Alemán. Este jueves, el guardameta expresó en un extenso comunicado publicado en sus redes sociales que decidió "no iniciar acciones judiciales ni presentar denuncias" contra el árbitro. "Mi intención es dar por superado este episodio y evitar que esta situación continúe generando conflictos, sin dejar de estar a plena disposición de las autoridades competentes para cualquier aclaración que corresponda", agregó el arquero de 29 años. Por el momento, no hubo ningún pronunciamiento del árbitro, de la directiva de Real Potosí ni de la Federación Boliviana de Fútbol (FBF) sobre el incidente. La Copa Bolivia es un torneo por series y es el segundo más importante de la División Profesional del país, después de la liga que todavía está en disputa, con la batalla por el liderato entre el Bolívar de La Paz y el campeón defensor, Always Ready, ambos con 60 puntos, a falta de tres fechas para su conclusión. El título de la Copa Bolivia otorga al vencedor el cupo de Bolivia 3 en la fase previa de la Copa Libertadores, algo que puede cambiar en este caso si el equipo millonario finaliza la liga en primer o segundo lugar, con lo que logrará su pase a la etapa de grupos.

articles.title: Vinicius, con la amenaza de Diomande
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Los dos últimos partidos de Vinicius (la media hora final ante el Celta, completo ante el PSV), dan a ver a un Vinicius en recuperación. Los dos partidos con Brasil en Singapur (dos y tres goles respectivamente, ante Japón primero y ante la selección local después), le han dado seguridad. Y una distancia para la reflexión con un propósito de enmienda expresado al confesar que había estado entrenando poco. La irrupción de Diomande le ha hecho ver las orejas al lobo, ha vuelto, se ve, al trabajo duro, y se le ha notado más rápido y atrevido. Aún no es el de sus mejores días, pero vuelve a ser un extremo peligroso y útil. Y todos podemos recordar su techo como jugador de ataque, que está por encima del que hasta ahora le hemos visto a Diomande. Aunque este ha agradado mucho, desde luego. Pero hablamos de ataque. En lo otro, la solidaridad y el esfuerzo defensivo, no hay color. La media hora contra el Celta era ideal para Vinicius, porque se iba a jugar en medio campo, con el rival acorralado. Lo mismo ocurrió en la segunda mitad ante el PSV, pero no en la primera, cuando a campo total le vimos una y otra vez desentendido de Dest, con la consecuencia de desajustes y jugadas de peligro en el área de Courtois. En ese aspecto Diomande es impecable. Y queda una tercera cuestión a considerar: las protestas, la facilidad para meterse en líos. Cero que en esto se va corrigiendo, al compás que se han ido esfumando los insultos racistas en gran parte gracias a él y a su gallarda actitud aquel día en Mestalla, pero aún le siguen sobrando desplantes. Se resalta, incluso como un elogio, que los compañeros le quieren ayudar, y es verdad, y lo mismo Mourinho, que no iba a desperdiciar un jugador así. Pero las soluciones tienen que salir de él, mejorando todavía más sus prestaciones en ataque, que puede, pero sobre todo tomándose en serio el papel de jugador integral que exige el fútbol de hoy, donde vemos a máximas figuras retrocediendo con velocidad cuando la situación lo exige.

articles.title: Dos 'cohetes' hacia Primera división
articles.standfirst: Almería y Castellón disparan sus opciones de ascenso tras un inicio histórico y empiezan a dejar atrás al resto de candidatos
articles.summary: Almería y Castellón disparan sus opciones de ascenso tras un inicio histórico y empiezan a dejar atrás al resto de candidatos
articles.body: La Segunda división comienza a tener dos claros protagonistas. Almería y Castellón no solo ocupan las dos primeras posiciones de la clasificación, sino que empiezan a abrir una brecha con el resto de aspirantes al ascenso directo. Tras 15 jornadas, el conjunto de García Pimienta aventaja en ocho puntos al tercer clasificado, el Girona, mientras que los ‘orelluts’ le sacan seis, con un partido menos. Es cierto que el Granada, también con 27 puntos, tiene pendiente su partido ante el Tenerife y podría reducir esa distancia, aunque la sensación es que ambos líderes han impuesto un ritmo que nadie consigue seguir. El Almería lidera la tabla con 35 puntos y atraviesa un momento sencillamente espectacular. Encadena 12 jornadas sumando, con un balance de 10 victorias y dos empates, y no conoce la derrota desde finales de agosto. El Castellón, por su parte, suma 33 puntos, aunque con un encuentro menos que deberá recuperar frente al Eibar. Además, solo ha perdido uno de sus 14 partidos, hace más de un mes ante el Andorra, y enlaza ya cinco jornadas invicto. Lo verdaderamente llamativo es que ambos clubes están firmando el mejor arranque liguero de toda su historia, tanto en Primera como en Segunda división. Nunca antes habían alcanzado semejante puntuación a estas alturas del campeonato, un dato que refleja la dimensión del inicio de temporada de los dos conjuntos. En el caso del Almería, además, la estadística invita al optimismo. Desde que las victorias valen tres puntos, únicamente el Elche en la temporada 2012-13 y el Cádiz en la 2019-20 habían alcanzado los 35 puntos tras 15 jornadas... y ambos terminaron ascendiendo a Primera. Solo el Racing de Santander mejoró esa cifra en la campaña 2024-25, pero acabó quedándose sin el ascenso. Las proyecciones también disparan la ilusión. Si mantienen el ritmo actual, tanto Almería como Castellón finalizarían el campeonato cerca de la barrera de los 100 puntos, un registro reservado para temporadas históricas. Y el calendario ya tiene marcada en rojo la próxima gran cita. El 6 de diciembre, a las 16:15 horas, Castalia acogerá un apasionante Castellón-Almería con el liderato en juego. Un duelo entre los dos equipos más en forma de la categoría que puede reforzar la escapada rojiblanca o dar un vuelco a la cabeza de la clasificación, especialmente teniendo en cuenta que los albinegros aún tienen un partido pendiente.

articles.title: Escándalo en Londres: un aficionado empujó a Jon Martín en pleno partido
articles.standfirst: "Es una de las imágenes de la noche de la Europa League"
articles.summary: "Es una de las imágenes de la noche de la Europa League"
articles.body: Jon Martín, el poderoso y joven defensa de la Real Sociedad, fue doble protagonista de la derrota del equipo donostiarra por 2-1 contra el Crystal Palace en la Europa League. El futbolista de Lasarte-Oria fue empujado por un aficionado en pleno partido, y 15 minutos después fue expulsado al ver la segunda amarilla tras un controvertido penalti que le pitó el árbitro noruego Rohit Saggi. Jon Martín le gana la posición a Nketiah en un duelo defensivo... ¡y un aficionado del Crystal Palace empujó a Jon Martín en el pecho para recriminárselo desde la grada del fondo! El programa 'La Casa del Fútbol' de Movistar Plus Deportes definió la acción del aficionado contra el jugador de la Real Sociedad como "una de las imágenes de la noche de la Europa League". En el minuto 70 el árbitro expulsó a Jon Martín tras un forcejeo con Mateta en el área. "Estoy jodido, porque creo que el equipo ha hecho un gran partido y que hasta el minuto 70 hemos sido mejores en todas las facetas del juego, que ellos no nos han generado casi y que nosotros las hemos tenido como para adelantarnos con más ventaja, pero en la acción del penalti cambia todo, porque es el penalti y el equipo se queda con uno menos", declaró Jon Martín tras el partido. Jon Martín considera que su jugada con Mateta es "una acción muy dudosa", y explica que "los dos disputamos el balón dentro del área, yo tengo los brazos sobre él, pero en ningún momento le agarro, sino que él va cayendo hacia atrás. Me sorprende, sobre todo, que se piten tan rápido estas acciones que perjudican a un equipo, que hay un VAR para poder ir a verlas y después, si lo ves así, pitas penalti, pero el árbitro en cinco o 10 segundos ha dicho que estaba confirmado".

articles.title: La conexión 'made in' La Masia que es oro para España
articles.standfirst: Sergi Mayans y Ebrima Tunkara explican a MARCA cómo su complicidad en La Masia resultó decisiva para superar a Marruecos
articles.summary: Sergi Mayans y Ebrima Tunkara explican a MARCA cómo su complicidad en La Masia resultó decisiva para superar a Marruecos
articles.body: Sergi Mayans y Ebrima Tunkara llevan tiempo aprendiendo a entenderse. Uno desde la defensa, el otro muchos metros más adelante. Dos futbolistas de La Masia que comparten algo más que una camiseta y que han encontrado en la selección española el escenario para llevar su complicidad a otra dimensión. Mayans, central con una facilidad especial para encontrar compañeros donde otros apenas distinguen espacios. Tunkara, un atacante que vive de descubrirlos antes que nadie. Dos maneras distintas de interpretar el fútbol que terminan encontrándose en el mismo lugar. Y una conexión que se ha convertido en una de las armas de una España que avanza con autoridad por el Mundial Sub-17. El entendimiento entre ambos no necesita demasiadas explicaciones. Se ha construido entre entrenamientos y partidos en el Barcelona, donde han aprendido a reconocer los movimientos del otro. Una asociación que ante Marruecos permitió fabricar el primer gol del encuentro, aunque la jugada empezó bastante antes de que el balón llegara a la portería. "Nos entendemos porque la jugada anterior ya la había visto. En medio del partido me ha hablado y me ha dicho: 'Mírame, porque no me están siguiendo'. He visto que se desmarcaba y se la he dado", explicó Mayans a MARCA. El propio Tunkara confirmó que aquella conversación forma parte de una costumbre compartida: "En el Barça también, cuando juega conmigo, nos comunicamos así. Le digo que me tire balones a la espalda porque el central está un poco despistado". Y así ocurrió. Mayans levantó la cabeza desde la defensa y encontró a Tunkara con un desplazamiento que dejó atrás a la zaga marroquí. El extremo había detectado el espacio antes de que apareciera el pase. Controló para orientarse y, con el siguiente toque, resolvió con la zurda. Dos gestos que bastaron para superar al guardameta y abrir el marcador. La jugada había comenzado con una advertencia y terminó convertida en gol. Una acción que condensó buena parte de las virtudes de ambos futbolistas y permitió a España tomar ventaja en su primer encuentro de verdadera exigencia. Marruecos había intentado imponer un partido físico, de contactos constantes, pero encontró en aquella sociedad azulgrana un problema que no supo resolver. Tunkara fue, además, uno de los grandes protagonistas de la tarde. Los defensores marroquíes lo persiguieron durante buena parte del encuentro, con entradas que trataron de interrumpir sus carreras y limitar su influencia. No lo consiguieron. El atacante volvió a demostrar su capacidad para superar rivales y dejó una acción en la que desbordó a tres defensores antes de servir una ocasión a Yeremaiah. Su actuación le valió el reconocimiento al mejor jugador del partido, aunque él apenas concedió importancia al premio. "Es un reconocimiento de que has hecho un buen partido, pero más que eso no es nada. Lo importante es llegar a la final y ganar el Mundial", aseguró. Una declaración que retrata la ambición de un futbolista que, a sus 16 años, ya mira mucho más allá de los reconocimientos individuales. Mayans, por su parte, continúa consolidándose como un defensa que entiende su trabajo más allá de la recuperación del balón. Su capacidad para iniciar el juego y encontrar soluciones desde atrás ha provocado comparaciones con Pau Cubarsí, otro producto de La Masia. "Ojalá. Yo creo que me parezco bastante en ese aspecto y ojalá poder ser un gran jugador como él", reconoció el central. Aunque sus referentes son Aymeric Laporte e Iñigo Martínez, dos defensas acostumbrados a convertir la salida de balón en una herramienta ofensiva. El pase a Tunkara ante Marruecos fue una muestra de esa personalidad. Mayans tampoco esconde las aspiraciones de España: "Creo que podemos ser candidatos a ganarlo. El entrenador nos lo dice mucho y, si jugamos así, creo que podemos ser los ganadores". España ha cerrado la fase de grupos con tres victorias, 22 goles a favor y ninguno en contra. Una superioridad que ahora tendrá que trasladar a las eliminatorias, donde cada error puede tener consecuencias definitivas. Cubillo dispone de talento, alternativas y una generación que parece haber encontrado una manera compartida de entender el juego. Pero también de pequeñas sociedades que se han construido lejos de Catar y que pueden terminar resolviendo partidos cuando las diferencias sean mínimas.

articles.title: Neville: "Haaland será jugador del Madrid en un plazo máximo de 18 meses"
articles.standfirst: Gary Neville pronostica que el Real Madrid venderá a Vinicius y fichará a Haaland para formar una delantera con Mbappé
articles.summary: Gary Neville pronostica que el Real Madrid venderá a Vinicius y fichará a Haaland para formar una delantera con Mbappé
articles.body: Gary Neville, mito del Manchester United y exentrenador del Valencia (2015–2016), ha declarado en el podcast 'The Overlap' que "estoy absolutamente seguro de que Erling Haaland será jugador del Real Madrid en un plazo máximo de 18 meses, quizá al final de la temporada". Haaland, que acaba contrato con el Manchester City en 2034 y que actualmente está inmerso en una batalla legal con un electricista polaco, fue la principal baza del candidato Enrique Riquelme en la campaña electoral por la presidencia del Madrid que acabó ganando Florentino Pérez. Alfie Haaland, el padre de Haaland, ya se dejó querer por el equipo merengue: "Erling está contento en el City, tiene un contrato largo... pero cualquier jugador quiere jugar en el Real Madrid". Gary Neville apuesta por una delantera formada por Erling Haaland y Kylian Mbappé en el Real Madrid, a la vez que se plante la salida de Vinicius del Bernabéu. "Creo que Vinicius se marchará del Real Madrid, Mbappé pasará a la banda izquierda y Haaland será el delantero centro del Real Madrid", pronosticó el exfutbolista de 51 años en una declaraciones que están dando la vuelta al mundo futbolístico. La sanción que recibirá el Manchester City por su irregularidades financieras podría precipitar la salida de muchas de sus figuras del Etihad Stadium. La IA predice que el Real Madrid podría fichar a Haaland, con el F.C. Barcelona a la expectativa, y a otros siete jugadores del Manchester City (Enzo Fernández, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Phil Foden, Abdukodir Khusanov, Vitor Reis, Josko Gvardiol y Mateo Kovacic). Por el momento Haaland se mantiene fiel al City y no teme el posible descenso de los 'citizens': "Firmé un contrato de nueve años y medio".

articles.title: French, Bulgarian presidents slam Marseille violence, five fans in hospital
articles.summary: French and Bulgarian presidents slam Marseille fans after violent scenes in UEFA Europa League match with Levski Sofia.
articles.body:
Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans.

The lead-up to the match at the Stade Velodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares.

French President Emmanuel Macron condemned “in the strongest possible terms … acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans”, the Elysee Palace said.

Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova called it “unacceptable” and “shocking”.

“The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world,” she said in a statement on Facebook.

“Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety.”

Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that “these acts would not go unpunished”, the Elysee said.

Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Levski supporters.

They breached the stand designated for away fans, where about 500 visiting fans were gathered.

Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings.

“Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” a source with the Marseille police prefecture told the AFP news agency.

“Six others were treated on site for various wounds.”

The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was “no information at this stage regarding any arrests”.

Manuel Bompard, an MP for the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party for Marseille’s Bouches-du-Rhone department, commented on a video shared online purporting to show a Levski fan performing a Nazi salute.

“The far right has no place in our stadiums!” he wrote on X.

Iotova called on French authorities to “clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them”.

She urged European football’s governing body UEFA to “check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured”.

“We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!” she said.

Security personnel eventually restored calm as the game kicked off on time.

Another flare-up between opposing fans occurred at halftime, before the match ended 1-0 to the hosts.

“It’s a very regrettable episode – these are incidents which are unacceptable for football,” said Levski coach Julio Velazquez.

“I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I’m very saddened by this situation.”

Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was “working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents”.

“We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable,” said Marseille coach Bruno Genesio.

articles.title: Jamal Musiala: What next for Bayern Munich star?
articles.summary: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala might never return to his previous level and will deal with a medical condition for the rest of his life. What happens next?
articles.body:
Bayern Munich - and representatives of one of their most prominent players -have collided over recent weeks.

During the summer, the public became aware that their star 23-year-old midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered from absence seizures.

This neurological condition causes a brief, sudden lapse in awareness and responsiveness. Musiala had two of these lapses during pre-season games, but episodes already happened during the previous year.

At first, the shock among fans and observers was huge. Bayern kept Musiala's condition a secret for some time, and only a few insiders knew about it. In the days after Musiala's lapse during a friendly against Heidenheim, speculations arose over whether the player's medical issue had been known before he signed a highly lucrative contract extension in February 2025.

But it has been confirmed by sources close to the team - and Bayern themselves - that the condition had not been detected before April 2025. One source described Musiala, at the time of signing his new contract, as being "in great health".

In April 2025, days after suffering a muscle tear, Musiala caused a high-speed car crash which cost him his driver's licence. Munich's public prosecutor's office responded to a recent enquiry saying there is no evidence that the accident was caused by a lapse, nor that it was the cause of Musiala's condition.

Nevertheless, checks a couple of days after the crash revealed he was suffering from absence seizures. Musiala's camp consulted numerous experts and hired doctors to treat the player, with the knowledge of Jochen Hahne, Bayern's team doctor. How close the consultations between the external doctors and Bayern's medical staff are remains a point of discussion, among many other things in this complex matter.

Soon after, Musiala's football-related injuries became an issue. He broke his fibula and injured his ankle during the Fifa Club World Cup after colliding with then PSG goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. He needed months to recover and suffered a subsequent ankle injury, likely related to the leg injury.

After the 2026 World Cup he had a metal plate removed from his left foot, which affected his pre-season preparation. Musiala just recently recovered from a weeks-long absence due to a hamstring tear.

On top of that, new incidents related to his neurological condition have come to light. Days before his recent return to training Musiala had another lapse, just like he did on the morning of a Champions League game against Real Madrid in April.

All of this is the tragic story of a highly talented footballer who might never return to his previous level and must deal with a medical condition for the rest of his life.

Absence seizures require daily medication. There are other high-level athletes, such as England rugby union player Tommy Freeman, who have had to deal with the same condition.

A controversy erupted last Friday, as Bayern faced Cologne in what was supposed to be an ordinary league game. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, once chairman of the board and now a member of Bayern's supervisory board, asked a TV crew to come to his section in the stands.

The unscheduled post-game interview unfolded in a way that no-one at Bayern, not even other members of the club's hierarchy, expected.

"He has a health issue, which is known, and it is known that he has a contract which includes hefty sums of money," Rummenigge said. "You need to talk to the family, to the player and most importantly to the agency, because these sums are - with all due respect - not justifiable any longer."

A day later, chairman of the board Jan-Christian Dreesen and club president Herbert Hainer tried to defuse the situation at the yearly membership assembly, but were also attacked by club member Jonathan Hoffmann.

Hoffmann, a neurologist, said it wouldn't help to go after Musiala publicly, for which he received applause from many of the present members.

One might wonder why an experienced deal-maker like Rummenigge would willingly put down one of his players who could still be valuable to the club, even if it's just for a sale.

He might have been agitated by the way the home game against Cologne went. Harry Kane suffered a ligament tear in his ankle early in the game and star winger Michael Olise had to leave the stadium on crutches.

But, even more importantly, it has become clear that Rummenigge was unhappy with how contract negotiations with Musiala's camp - between October 2024 and February 2025 - unfolded.

Bayern and particularly Max Eberl, the club's director of sport, were running out of time, as Musiala's contract would have ended with the conclusion of the 2025-26 season. If they hadn't reached an agreement before April or May 2025, Bayern would have felt obliged to sell Musiala during the summer transfer window.

Bayern under pressure during contract negotiations

Musiala played an impressive Euro 2024 for Germany and was one of Bayern's best players during the period of negotiations. Among others, Real Madrid were interested, but only for a free transfer in 2026.

Keep in mind, Musiala has quite a unique profile as a No 10 that can also come from the wing and break down low-block defences with his dribbles and passing.

Under pressure and confronted by a shrewd negotiator in Christian Schmid, Musiala's agent and a trained lawyer, Bayern agreed to a salary package that could earn Musiala, in a best-case scenario, £21m a year, with £15m as a base salary. Bayern also agreed to grant a signing fee of close to £25m, paid over the stretch of the contract. Musiala even got his wish granted of receiving his own box at Allianz Arena.

Some reports indicated that the fact Musiala's deal includes sick pay for six months, in the case of injury or illness, could be interpreted as circumstantial evidence that the player's representatives may have known about his condition beforehand. A standard Bundesliga contract only offers sick pay for six weeks before insurance would shoulder the payments.

But even six months is a short period in comparison. Premier League players receive their full basic wage for the first 18 months. And, when Bayern negotiate with top players, they ultimately compete against Europe's elite.

Rummenigge, and to a lesser extent his long-time boardroom compatriot Uli Hoeness, made Eberl responsible for the unfavourable terms - arguing that Schmid essentially played Eberl.

Eberl has been the target of criticism from the two former powerbrokers for quite some time. At a recent supervisory board meeting, Hoeness is said to have attacked Eberl for his inactivity over the Musiala issue in the past six months.

That being said, Bayern bought into the Musiala hype for a couple of years, hoping that they would have a superstar of their own who could be marketed across the globe.

The relationship between the club and agent Schmid has been strained to say the least, with Rummenigge particularly disliking him. Some sources believe this was one of the root causes for Rummenigge's recent attack on live TV.

When a 16-year-old Kennet Eichhorn came on the market during the summer, as he wanted to leave second-division side Hertha Berlin, Bayern were interested but ultimately dropped out of the race for the highly touted midfielder. Eichhorn is represented by Schmid and ended up joining Bayer Leverkusen.

Hoeness met with Schmid during the summer to discuss how to proceed with Musiala, but the player's agent did not indicate that they would agree to a wage reduction. Hoeness called the matter a "dilemma" for Bayern during a TV show earlier this month, but did not go as far as Rummenigge.

As long as Musiala is not medically forced to retire, he will receive the wage that was agreed upon in February 2025. Even if Bayern would intend to part ways with the player, they would need to do everything in their power to get the player as close to his previous form as possible.

The release clause of £125m, which could be triggered next year, seems unrealistic. Any comments by Bayern bosses against Musiala, or further leaks to the media, may indeed lower his market value down to zero - unless the player can simply shake things off and perform again.

Eberl and head coach Vincent Kompany have come out to back Musiala. Joshua Kimmich, one of Bayern's veteran players, also criticised the treatment of Musiala after a 2-1 loss to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. "Of course, the club is above all and bigger than the player, but not bigger than the human. This is an absolute no-go and also not Bayern-like," Kimmich said.

Even football players' union Fifpro condemned Rummenigge's comments. On Wednesday, Bayern put out a statement saying that a meeting between the club and Musiala's representatives took place on Tuesday, in which it was agreed that the player's health should be paramount.

Whether the damage can be repaired is up in the air. As Bayern have a number of attacking players sidelined, they need a healthy and mentally prepared Musiala in the coming weeks and months.

articles.title: FPL gameweek 12 tips: Is it time to sell Man City's Erling Haaland?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert Holly Shand gives her answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers in gameweek 12.
articles.body:
The Premier League heads into another big weekend and BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert Holly Shand gives her answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek 12.

Erling Haaland (£15.8m) has blanked in three consecutive games for Manchester City , who have taken just one point in this period. More than 100,000 managers have transferred Haaland out this week, despite him being the most owned player in the game. Form and fixtures collide, with league leaders Arsenal up next.

He has a good record against the Gunners, scoring in their last four Premier League meetings. Additionally, I believe Haaland will be the best captain pick in the game for his next three home games against Leeds United , Chelsea and Hull City so I recommend holding the highest-scoring forward in the game.

Who is the best captain for Gameweek 12?

With Haaland's appeal dwindling this week, there are other options to consider across our squads. Bruno Fernandes (£11.6m) leads the data informed approach, as Manchester United entertain Brentford for Mauricio Pochettino's first game at Old Trafford. Are you brave enough to back the new manager bounce?

Elsewhere, Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) faces Coventry at home, scoring in three of his last five at Elland Road, while Nicolas Jackson (£7.5m) travels to Ipswich Town , with four goal involvements in four. Or could it be a week to back a defender with Brighton 's Maxim De Cuyper (£5.5m) ? He's the highest-scoring player in the game!

Should you play Free Hit in Gameweek 12?

If you own four of more players from Arsenal and Manchester City , then there's a strong case to play the Free Hit in Gameweek 12 to avoid that fixture. Back Leeds and Brighton defences, at home to Coventry and Newcastle respectively with James Trafford (£5.1m) , Tarik Muharemovic (£5.1m) , Luka Vuskovic (£5.3m) and De Cuyper.

Liverpool are among the form sides, with Florian Wirtz (£7.4m) and Alexander Isak (£9.1m) worth considering. Wirtz has hit a double digit return in his last two games. There's also places in the midfield for top performers Marcus Tavernier (£6.8m) and Pascal Gross (£6.3m) .

Cole Palmer has just one goal in his last five games which has frustrated his owners, and he picked up a red card in that period too. Chelsea 's attack has struggled to find the same intensity with Joao Pedro out injured, scoring just three goals in this time.

While Palmer's time in our squads is coming to a close, he is nailed on for 90 minutes in a congested period of games, with Chelsea not involved in Europe. He deserves the benefit of the doubt with Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace up next. Liverpool in Gameweek 14 is the obvious exit point.

The news coming out of Arsenal is still mixed on the fitness of the highest-owned goalkeeper in the game David Raya (£6.3m) . We do know he is not believed to need surgery, which means he is not expected to be out long term. He's probably a hold.

If news arrives he will only miss Gameweek 12, you could Free Hit, or go without a goalkeeper if your substitute goalkeeper is non-playing. Spurs ' Antonin Kinsky (£4.4m) leads the way for possible back-ups, with games against Sunderland and Fulham in the immediate schedule.

It is worth noting there is just 48 hours between Gameweek 12 drawing to a close and the midweek Gameweek 13 deadline, coming on Tuesday, 1 December at 6:30pm GMT. Set those alarms so that you don't miss any action over the congestion in the next six weeks!

Be mindful that we might see increased rotation in the midweek rounds, particularly for wingers and full-backs. Those sides already involved in Europe are more likely to rotate, so having a strong bench in these instances could be key.

Also look out for players who are on four bookings, like Tavernier and Gross, as another yellow card could result in a one-match ban.

articles.title: La gran remontada de Bernardo Silva
articles.standfirst: El portugués, que llegó corto de forma, ahora es pìeza clave en la racha victoriosa del Madrid
articles.summary: El portugués, que llegó corto de forma, ahora es pìeza clave en la racha victoriosa del Madrid
articles.body: “Bernardo es un jugador muy importante para nosotros, pero el pobre es otro de esos a los que les gusta no hacer nada durante las vacaciones. Le viene bien mentalmente no hacer nada en su tiempo libre, así que ha vuelto en baja forma física; tiene que mejorar”. José Mourinho pronunció estas palabras sobre Bernardo SIlva en la pretemporada, concretamente a principios de agosto, tras el amistoso de preparación ante el Ferencvaros en Budapest. Unas palabras que llamaron la atención por lo directo de la crítica, pero que reafirmaron la buena conexión personal entre el técnico y el jugador. De hecho, Mou fue determinante para que Bernardo se decantara por la oferta del Real Madrid tras quedar libre de contrato en el Manchester City. Un movimiento que captó la atención de varios clubes, incluidos el Barcelona y el Atlético de Madrid. De hecho, ambos se vieron cerca de lograr la contratación del luso, que lo paró todo en cuanto tuvo conocimiento de la oferta del Madrid, avalada por Mou. Con todo, las dudas de la pretemporada tuvieron continuidad con el arranque del curso oficial. Bernardo, pieza clave en el mejor City de la historia, no acababa de encontrar su sitio en el Real Madrid. Mou apostó de inicio por un doble pivote más físico, con Valverde y Tchouaméni como primeras opciones en la mayor parte de los partidos. Bernardo no tenía sitio, pero esperó pacientemente su oportunidad. Ésta llegó en Roma, cuando el técnico le dio 20 minutos para buscar la primera gran remontada del Madrid en esta Champions. Mou juntó a Silva con Güler y retrasó a Fede al lateral para hacer hueco a los jugones en el centro del campo. La fórmula funcionó porque el Madrid ganó el partido (del 3-1 al 3-4), pero el entrenador del Madrid no acababa de ver claro ese doble pivote de corte tan creativo, pero escaso de físico. “Si hubiera jugado de inicio con Arda y Bernardo, la Roma nos hubiera metido cinco”, dijo el técnico en la sala de prensa del Olímpico. Ese partido se jugó el 14 de octubre. Una semana después, ante el Leipizig, Bernardo era titular, anotando además su único gol de la temporada hasta ahora. Pero la prueba de fuego llegó el 21 de octubre en el Camp Nou. Bernardo y Arda fueron titulares y el Madrid ganó al Barcelona para recuperar terreno en la pelea por la Liga. Un partido en el que Bernardo volvió a ser el pulmón silencioso del Madrid. Porque Bernardo no sólo juega. El luso corre, y mucho, haciendo gala de ese motor que, en el arranque de la temporada, estaba falto de rodaje. Además de dar criterio a la salida del balón, la mezcla de Bernardo con Arda y Fede ha generado una nueva estructura en el centro del campo del Real Madrid. Con el capitán como falso lateral, es habitual ver a los medios del Madrid aparecer en lugares inesperados por sus rivales. La movilidad es clave, y sirve de distracción ante los rivales para que los atacantes encuentren más espacios y puedan explotar mejor sus virtudes. Con un Bernardo Silva cada vez más parecido a ese jugador omnipresente del City, el Madrid cabalga con brío. Son diez vitorias para un equipo que parece haber encontrado la fórmula de la Coca-Cola futbolistica.

articles.title: What makes or breaks a high press?
articles.summary: A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football, but what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season?
articles.body:
A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention.

When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart.

So, what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season?

When a team decides to press, they must first establish their intention. This informs how the players act.

Speaking to DAZN Portugal , Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about whether a good press relied more on physicality or courage.

"When you want to press high you need the courage and mindset to do it. Our mindset is we press to score, we don't just press to win the ball back."

In coaching, clarity is key - particularly when it comes to creating alignment in the squad and Hurzeler is deliberate in simplifying big ideas when delivering messages to his players, a skill he practised as a radio pundit during the World Cup.

"[Punditry] helps you as a coach in that you have to summarise things in a short and easy way so that everyone understands," he said. "Football might get more complex but simplicity counts."

Hurzeler's "pressing to score" is a phrase that communicates many ideas in a memorable three words: intensity, being proactive, and immediate forward-thinking on winning the ball.

It also frames pressing in a way that makes it easy for attackers to buy into, in the form of goals.

"You want commitment from everyone on the pitch," Hurzeler explained.

"If just one has doubts, the whole press is gone."

The Red Bull school of coaching uses a similarly succinct phrase - "the last step" to address these ideas around intention, collectiveness and aggression.

Summarised by Tactx , whose coaches have worked under the Red Bull model, the last step refers to "players [being] coached to attack through the opponent, using the final step to lunge aggressively at the ball".

"This action commits the defender fully and is often the decisive moment that allows possession to be won."

Pressing to engage rather than just to close distances ensures the team in possession aren't given the time or space to play through otherwise half-hearted pressure.

2. Knowing when to press and when to drop off

When discussing how good or bad a team is at pressing, how much they run is often brought up. But the distance a team covers fails to paint the full picture when it comes to the effectiveness of a team's pressing strategy.

Liverpool 's current boss Andoni Iraola was asked about how he interpreted physical data last year.

"It's not 'we run a lot, so we are good,' no," he said. "The high-speed running, the sprint speeds [matter for us] - not total distance covered.

"[Some] teams that do not run a lot get very good results because they have [their] way of playing."

Sprints matter more than distance covered for Iraola's side, who have clear ideas of how to press, looking to win the ball back through a sudden and intense pressure from familiar positions they are well prepared for.

If the conditions to implement this press aren't on, the wingers can be seen dropping off, forming a more compact defensive shape with the likes of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz defending in a front two for longer periods of the match.

It's smart. Liverpool look to maximise the effectiveness of when they do press, with full commitment expected in each sprint, with players conserving their energy in moments a press is less likely to succeed.

With pressing being a front-footed idea, coaches may throw caution to the wind but this can leave them exposed in ways teams have become better at exploiting.

Hurzeler touched on the need for balance when pressing.

"I always say in certain moments you need to have the courage to take risk but you need to have the discipline to control the risk," he said.

For Brighton , this looks like certain players abandoning man-to-man marking when their respective attacker attempts to drag them into awkward positions.

Instead, Brighton will protect the centre of the pitch on top of their man-to-man principles which helps them stay compact.

When the defending side aren't compact, spaces exist for the attacking side to target. When players step up to press, these gaps can arise in between the lines.

Again, Brighton manage to plug these gaps well by pressing hard, reducing the time opponents have to play passes into midfield, while also encouraging players to make vertical jumps up the pitch, covering players left by teammates who have pressed higher up the pitch.

When teams lack vertical compactness - not pressing with enough intensity and without making the necessary steps up the pitch - the space left in midfield has been exploited by clever sides, such as Leeds .

In their 4-1 loss to Daniel Farke's men, Chelsea looked to press high, with attackers and midfielders running up the pitch to apply pressure.

But when the ball went back the other way, these same players struggled.

The idea behind playing over a team's press isn't always to make the ball stick at the feet of a target man, although this helps. Instead space is found in the gaps between the pressing side's lines.

Recognising when teammates are likely to win headers or clip the ball forwards, midfielders are able to turn and run in the direction the ball is heading in, positioned ready to win second balls in numbers.

By comparison, the pressing side's midfielders, having to apply forward pressure before turning around to track back are often slower to contest second balls.

4. Having a plan for pressing with a man less

By this point, it will be clear that pressing is influenced by countless variables but it is worth highlighting one final factor; teams need solutions when pressing with one fewer player than the attacking side.

This most obviously happens when the opposition goalkeeper is involved in build-up play.

Here, the team in possession have 11 options against the 10 pressing players.

Obvious solutions come in the form one of the forward attackers pressing a centre-back at an angle which usually forces them to pass it back to the goalkeeper.

At that point, the same pressing player will continue his run, now pressing the keeper.

By curving their run and pressing at an angle, the idea is that the keeper will struggle to pass it back to the now unmarked centre-back.

This is generally true but again, good teams have found smart solutions to access this player.

One solution comes when the keeper passes the ball into a central player who then bounces the pass into the unmarked centre-back. This comes with risk given that the central player is usually marked. But sudden darts towards the ball can give them the time and space to play the bounce pass required.

A riskier but more impressive solution is when the keeper is willing and able to avoid the opponents attempt to force him in one direction, instead playing the ball back the other way themselves.

Queens Park Rangers' Pierce Charles, on loan from Manchester City , has done this better than most in world football, and his quality was clearest against Swansea's excellent press.

By playing against the direction of Swansea's press, to his unmarked teammate, he was able to immediately disorganise their press.

Changes in how a team presses force teams to innovate their build-up play which in turn force teams to innovate in how they press. It's a cycle that spins at a blistering pace, especially in the Premier League.

Given the detailed analysis and constant adaptation, teams and coaches in 2026 can ill-afford to rest on their laurels.

articles.title: La caída de Heskey: bancarrota, deudas, un amargo divorcio... y ahora vende golosinas con cannabis
articles.standfirst: Emile Heskey, ahogado por la bancarrota, sus deudas con Hacienda y un amargo divorcio, ha acabado inmerso en el controvertido mundo de comercialización de sustancias con cannabis
articles.summary: Emile Heskey, ahogado por la bancarrota, sus deudas con Hacienda y un amargo divorcio, ha acabado inmerso en el controvertido mundo de comercialización de sustancias con cannabis
articles.body: Emile Heskey, el goleador que durante varios lustros fue la gran esperanza del fútbol inglés (sumó 110 goles en la Premier League entre Leicester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Wigan y Aston Villa), ha pasado de ser una estrella de la selección de Inglaterra a vender en un almacén golosinas de cannabis de la marca Supreme CBD. El exfutbolista de 48 años promociona un bote de gominolas que contienen cannabidiol (CBD), un ingrediente legal pero controvertido derivado del cannabis, junto a otros famosos como Katie Price y exfutbolista Paul Merson (Arsenal). "Confío plenamente en estos productos para conciliar el sueño ¡Me han ido de maravilla desde hace años!", publica el propio Heskey, que fue 62 veces internacional con Inglaterra y disputó dos Mundiales, en Instagram. La vida después del fútbol ha sido bastante complicada para Emilie Heskey, que desde que se retiró en 2016 ha ocupado cargos en las categorías inferiores de la selección inglesa y en el equipo femenino del Leicester, además de colaborar ocasionalmente como comentarista en la BBC. En 2010 Emile Heskey, que acumuló un patrimonio de más de 15 millones de euros a lo largo de su carrera, se declaró en bancarrota. El futbolista se vio envuelto en una disputa legal relacionada con la adquisición —presuntamente fraudulenta y valorada en 16 millones de euros— del club chipriota Apollon Limassol por parte del empresario británico Craig Gabriel. Heskey había sido elegido para ser la cara visible de la operación y ocupar un puesto en la directiva del club. En 2023 se reveló que Heskey había dejado de pagar 110.000 euros en impuestos, correspondientes a su labor como responsable de desarrollo futbolístico entre 2017 y 2020. Fue sancionado con una multa de 50.000 euros. Ese mismo año el bar-restaurante Parea, financiado por él y gestionado por su esposa (Chantelle), fue liquidado por orden judicial, con una deuda acumulada de 194.000 euros. El restaurante acaparó titulares en 2019 cuando durante la fiesta de su primer aniversario se sirvió sushi sobre el cuerpo de una mujer semidesnuda, que yacía en una mesa con sus partes íntimas tapadas con trozos de salmón. En 2024 Heskey se enfrentó a nuevas dificultades financieras relacionadas con su participación en un esquema de inversión de Ingenious Media para celebridades, que se vio envuelto en una disputa fiscal de más de 1.900 millones de euros. David Beckham, Andrew Lloyd Webber, Gerrard, Jeremy Paxmany Robbie Williams también se vieron afectados. Ese año Heskey fue condenado a pagar 239.000 libras en el marco de un litigio relacionado con una deuda tributaria impagada de casi 2 millones de euros. Tras su debacle económica Emile Heskey se acabó distanciando de su esposa Chantelle, con la que se casó en 2014 y tiene cuatro hijos. Desde julio Heskey sale con Jade Slusarczyk, y desde que la pareja hizo pública su relación Chantelle inició los trámites de divorcio. En agosto de 2026 Chantelle calificó al exfutbolista como "despreciable".

articles.title: Paul Pogba urges Man Utd to copy Arsenal blueprint and stop living in the past after Mauricio Pochettino's nightmare start
articles.summary: Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Pogba has sent a clear message to his old club, urging them to abandon their obsession with past glories. As the Red...
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Pogba has sent a clear message to his old club, urging them to abandon their obsession with past glories. As the Red Devils endure a nightmare start to life under Mauricio Pochettino, the Frenchman believes the path back to the top lies in north London.

Crisis at Old Trafford sparks managerial change

Manchester United sit 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 games, leaving them in an early relegation battle. After failing to win a trophy across the past two seasons, the club sacked Michael Carrick during the international break.

Pochettino arrived to spark an immediate turnaround , yet his reign began with a heavy 4-0 loss to Liverpool. His side showed modest improvement on Wednesday night by earning a 2-2 Champions League draw away to Sporting.

Pogba backs Pochettino and urges patience

Speaking to talkSPORT , Pogba endorsed Pochettino's appointment while expressing sympathy for Carrick. He argued that the squad needs internal stability rather than another quick fix.

"I'm happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he's a great manager. And I'm sad also for Michael Carrick because I don't think he had enough time to show and prove himself," Pogba said. "But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there's a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win and we all think that they should change manager.

"All I think about this team, I've been there, is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside. Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things. The players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere, like Arsenal."

Why Arsenal's rebuild offers a blueprint

Pogba pointed to Mikel Arteta's rebuild at Arsenal as a model for his former club. Following their peak under Thierry Henry, the Gunners endured a long title drought before returning to contention.

"Arsenal had a great time with Thierry Henry. They had a great [era], they went to Champions League final, they won the Premier League. And they had a [long] time [before] winning again. It took how many years [between] the last time that Arsenal won the Premier League?" Pogba said. "But the pressure, I know it's a big club, it's Manchester United, was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

"And that's all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about them like they are the team that it was back then. You need to respect, you need to let them grow again and get back to the top."

Pochettino must quickly lift his squad out of the relegation zone after collecting just eight points from 11 league matches. Building on Wednesday's Champions League draw against Sporting will be vital as he works to implement his ideas and end a two-season trophy drought without the burden of past expectations.
