articles.title: Kahn praises Kimmich for defending Musiala: 'Important signal'
articles.summary: Former Bayern Munich chief executive Oliver Kahn has renewed his criticism of the club's leadership over its public handling of Jamal Musiala's health proble...
articles.body:
Former Bayern Munich chief executive Oliver Kahn has renewed his criticism of the club's leadership over its public handling of Jamal Musiala's health problems, while praising Joshua Kimmich for defending his team-mate.

"Joshua Kimmich has always been someone who speaks his mind," the former Bayern goalkeeper told RTL and Sky's "Triple" football talk show.

Kahn said it was important for Kimmich, Germany's national team captain, to stand by Musiala and send a message of unity to the squad during a difficult period.

"That was an important signal from Joshua," he said.

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have raised the possibility of Musiala taking a pay cut amid concerns over his health. They have also publicly questioned whether Musiala, 23, can return to his previous level of performance.

"I still don't understand why those statements were made. What has been achieved?" Kahn said. "Jamal has been weakened, he has been damaged to some extent. In a way, financial damage has also been done."

Kahn, who had criticized Hoeness over his remarks about two weeks ago, said the public debate risked unsettling Bayern's squad.

He suggested the remarks may have been intended to put pressure on Musiala's representatives but said such matters should be handled privately.

Musiala has been struggling with health problems and trying to regain his previous form for around 18 months.

Kimmich criticized Bayern's handling of the situation following Wednesday's 2-1 Champions League defeat at Lille, publicly defending his team-mate against comments made by senior club officials.

articles.title: Leaders BVB host in-form Leverkusen, Wounded HSV and Bayern clash, Englischen Wochen planning: Five things to look out for on Bundesliga Matchday 11
articles.summary: Before the Round of 16 DFB-Pokal midweek action, matchday 11 of the Bundesliga promised some intriguing fixtures. Here are the five talking points before Wer...
articles.body:
Before the Round of 16 DFB-Pokal midweek action, matchday 11 of the Bundesliga promised some intriguing fixtures. Here are the five talking points before Werder Bremen host bottom-placed Borussia Mönchengladbach in the opening fixture of the weekend's actions.

Dortmund face next big challenge after Arsenal draw

Days after returning to the Bundesliga summit, Borussia Dortmund became the first men's team to return home with a point from a visit to Emirates Stadium this season. Niko Kovač's men will have four more tricky fixtures in the space of 11 days.

In the middle of home games against Bayer Leverkusen and Inter, the Black and Yellows travel to Eintracht Frankfurt and fierce rivals Schalke. On Sunday night, Carles Martinez's men will hope to record their fourth successive win in all competitions.

In addition, it'll be their fourth win on the trot at Westfalenstadion (Signal Iduna Park) if they manage to end Dortmund's unbeaten start to the league campaign. Goals from Ibrahim Maza and Robert Andrich helped Die Werkself to upset BVB both in the DFB-Pokal and Bundesliga last term.

HSV fancy first win over Bayern in 17 years

Staying with the topic of unbeaten runs, Bayern's streak in all competitions came to an end on Wednesday as Vincent Kompany's depleted side lost at LOSC Lille. Uncharacteristically, the Rekordmeister have only managed two wins from their last five games.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's side lost four in five, including a 4-0 defeat to Nordderby rivals Werder Bremen last week. Miro Muheim suffering yet another serious injury compounded HSV's misery as they showed plenty of cracks in a shocking second-half performance at Weserstadion.

However, facing a Bayern side with plenty of their own issues present a perfect opportunity to end a 21-game winless run in this fixture. Since they beat Bayern twice in 2009 with Mladen Petric's goals, it has been a one-sided affair between the 1980s rivals. Last season's 2-2 draw at Volksparkstadion could also be used as a source of motivation for the hosts.

Overachievers Freiburg face attack-minded Leipzig

Freiburg extended their winning streak to six games with an injury-time triumph over Twente on Thursday. Julian Schuster's side are targeting an automatic qualification to the Round of 16 in the Conference League, while they face 2. Bundesliga side Kaiserslautern in the DFB-Pokal next Wednesday.

In the Bundesliga, they encounter a top-four clash on Sunday with RB Leipzig next to visit Europa-Park Stadion. Martin Demichelis' men scored five goals each in back-to-back league games before climbing to the top 24 in the Champions League with a 3-1 win over RC Lens. Brajan Gruda and Antonio Nusa will head to Freiburg with impressive form in front of goal.

Goal-shy Stuttgart host rejuvenated Eintracht Frankfurt

In a matchday packed with high-profile games, the Topspiel will be contested between two historic clubs in Stuttgart. Sebastian Hoeneß has a stacked squad in the final third, but they have only scored a single goal in their last four games in all competitions.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt are unbeaten in their last four matches as they climbed over their Saturday hosts with a narrow win in Hoffenheim last week. Nine goals were scored in the head-to-head games between the sides last term as Nikolas Nartey scored a late winner in a five-goal thriller in Stuttgart.

Both Ermedin Demirović and Deniz Undav were on target back then, and they will hope to end their respective goal droughts on Saturday. Adi Hütter's first win back as a Frankfurt coach came at Mainz, but that remains their only victory on the road in Bundesliga.

Dealing with back-to-back Englische Woche

For the sides in Europe, the last international break of the year followed with six games in the space of three weeks. The DFB-Pokal Round of 16 sandwiches the last two European matchdays of 2026 as the fixtures come thick and fast before the winterpause.

Usually, it's not something that worries FC Bayern, but the whole atmosphere at the club and injuries to key players made this the perfect time to face the juggernauts. Kompany's men will host 2. Bundesliga leaders Hertha after their tricky trip to Hamburg.

Stuttgart and Freiburg will also clash 2. Bundesliga teams, while Leverkusen and Frankfurt host Leipzig and Dortmund, respectively, in the standout fixtures of the round. Köln, Augsburg and Borussia Mönchengladbach need to find the right balance between a deep cup run and a relegation fight.

articles.title: Virgil van Dijk’s stance on staying amid interest from European giants
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk Contract Latest: Liverpool Captain Calm Amid Transfer InterestVirgil van Dijk’s future is moving into sharper focus, even if no final decisio...
articles.body:
Virgil van Dijk Contract Latest: Liverpool Captain Calm Amid Transfer Interest

Virgil van Dijk's future is moving into sharper focus, even if no final decision has yet been made. As reported by Daily Mail, the Liverpool captain has still not held formal talks over a new deal, and that naturally leaves room for speculation as the season progresses.

The centre-back, now 35, remains central to Liverpool despite the club managing his minutes more carefully. That has been evident in recent selection decisions, including his substitute outing in the Champions League win over Club Brugge. It does not point to diminished standing, far from it, but it does underline a broader reality. Liverpool are trying to balance Van Dijk's importance with the physical demands placed on one of the game's most influential defenders.

What stands out most is Van Dijk's composure. "The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," he told Sky Sports. "Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see."

He was equally firm in dismissing outside claims over his plans. "At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either."

That message feels significant. There is no public push, no grand declaration, only a player keeping his options open while making clear that performance remains the priority. "But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then."

There is also an acceptance that this story could still move in either direction. "But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years. If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

Interest from AC Milan has been mentioned, while Van Dijk is believed to be open to staying. For Liverpool, the next step is obvious. A player of this stature, leadership and consistency deserves clarity, and sooner rather than later.

This feels like one of those moments where Liverpool need to act with conviction. Van Dijk has earned that. Even with careful workload management, he still sets the tone on and off the pitch, and there are very few defenders in world football who bring his authority, calmness and leadership.

There is also something reassuring in how he has handled the situation. No drama, no noise, no pressure tactics. He has simply spoken like a senior professional who knows his value and understands timing. That should make Liverpool's decision easier, not harder.

Keeping him would still make plenty of sense. Experience matters, especially in a squad that may continue to evolve. Young defenders benefit from players like Van Dijk around them, and big matches still call for personalities who have seen everything before.

If this does become the final chapter, he will leave as one of the club's defining modern figures. But it still feels like there is more to give, and his own comments suggest he believes that too. Liverpool should not drift on this one. If the club see him as part of the immediate future, get the conversation moving and give everyone certainty. That would be the smart outcome.

articles.title: Misa Rodríguez: "Me esperaba mejor la despedida del Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: "Digo y hago lo que creo que define los valores que tengo"
articles.summary: "Digo y hago lo que creo que define los valores que tengo"
articles.body: Misa Rodríguez, guardameta de la selección española femenina de fútbol y del Arsenal, opinó en una entrevista con la agencia EFE durante la concentración del combinado nacional para los encuentros amistosos contra Chile, en León, y contra Venezuela, en A Coruña, que tanto ella como otras compañeras merecieron una despedida "mejor" del Real Madrid, su anterior club. "Una cosa no que me dolió pero que me esperaba mejor fue la despedida. Pero no solo la mía sino la de Tere Abelleira o la de jugadoras que han estado ahí desde el principio como Rocío o Weir. Pienso que merecimos una despedida mejor, pero fue bonita; todas las jugadoras lo hicieron bonito, la gente también lo hizo especial, vino a despedirse de nosotras. Me quedo con eso, que al final es lo importante", indicó la guardameta, que estuvo seis temporadas en el conjunto blanco y jugó allí 215 partidos. "Fueron días tristes porque llegaba ya al último partido de liga sabiendo que ya te vas a ir. Pero las jugadoras en ese momento nos reunimos todas, compramos flores, hicimos que ese momento fuese especial. Yo me quedo con eso, al final es lo bonito del fútbol, que las compañeras te despidan con tanto cariño y que el público también", indicó. De su paso por la entidad lo mejor que se lleva son las personas: "Siempre digo que lo mejor que te da el fútbol son las personas. En ese vestuario, Eva, Linda, Weir... conocer jugadoras que si no te las encuentras en el Real Madrid, a lo mejor no te las encuentras en otros clubes. Diría que las jugadoras, la amistad que he hecho con ellas". Preguntada acerca de si el Real Madrid dará algún día alcance al Barcelona, apuntó: "No sé, yo ya no estoy ahí. No sé qué tipo de proyecto hay, no sé nada ya. Les deseo todo lo mejor y que ojalá algún día lo consiga". En lo que respecta a la nueva etapa que ha iniciado en el Arsenal inglés, señaló: "La aclimatación está siendo muy buena, la verdad es que me gusta mucho la liga inglesa, es súper competitiva. Cada fin de semana los equipos te lo ponen muy difícil para conseguir los tres puntos, y lo estoy disfrutando". Misa no entra a analizar si otras compatriotas deberían orientar sus pasos hacia el fútbol inglés: "Lo único que les recomendaría es que estén donde quieran estar, donde se sientan bien, felices con su estilo de juego, ya sea en la liga española, en la alemana, en la brasileña en la inglesa... donde se sientan bien consigo mismas". Se acerca el final de su primer ciclo como campeonas del mundo. ¿Le viene mucho a la cabeza en su día a día el recuerdo de ese éxito? Ser campeonas del mundo queda ahí ya para la eternidad. Es verdad que quizás cuando estás en el club no lo piensas mucho, pero cuando vienes aquí, te miras en el pecho la estrella y dices, 'joder, que he sido campeona del Mundo'. En aquel Mundial empezó jugando y de repente dejó de hacerlo. ¿Ha tenido que trabajar mucho sobre ello a nivel mental para gestionar la frustración que debió generarle algo así?. En el fútbol pasan estas cosas y lo que te diferencia como una futbolista de alto rendimiento es el intentar mantener la calma y tener una mente fuerte en este sentido. Es verdad que hay momentos que cuestan, pero si algo he aprendido a lo largo de estos años y a raíz de la experiencia del Mundial es que, independientemente de lo que pase, tienes que seguir trabajando y dando lo mejor de ti. ¿Le convencieron las explicaciones que le dieron para tomar esa decisión? No hubo ninguna explicación, simplemente dejé de jugar y ya está. Ya está pasado, ya está superado, y yo sigo trabajando para dar lo mejor de mí cada día y también aquí en la Selección. Hubo una cosa un poco desagradable después y es que se empezó a insinuar que no era una buena compañera, que no aceptaba bien su suplencia. ¿Eso fue lo que más le dolió? No, porque como es una cosa que no es verdad, no le doy importancia a cosas que sé que no me definen como soy. La gente sabe como soy y todo lo contrario, te diría que intento hacer grupo, que me alegro de que a las porteras y a las jugadoras les vaya bien, porque si les va bien a ellas, significa que el equipo va a ir a bien. Hago oídos sordos a cosas que sé que no son verdad y que no dependen de mí. Estoy tranquila con eso. ¿Cree que detrás de todo aquello pudo haber estado el hecho de que fuese una de las figuras más representativas del Real Madrid? No, la verdad es que nunca he pensado '¿Por qué siempre es con la misma?'. Creo que tanto para bien como para mal soy una persona que soy muy transparente, siempre digo y hago lo que creo que define los valores que tengo y que me han inculcado en casa. No pienso que fuera por haber estado en el Real Madrid. Ahora hay un momento de paz en la selección española. ¿Cuánto ha costado llegar a algo así? Lo que haya costado o no al final ya ha pasado. Ahora creo que nos tenemos que centrar en que ya se han cerrado etapas, ciclos, y ahora estamos muy contentas con esta etapa de Sonia. Estamos muy contentas de poder tener una entrenadora de su calibre. ¿Es raro que le entrene alguien con quien ha jugado? No, no es raro. Además, yo de Sonia guardo un buen recuerdo en ese Atlético Madrid, me exigió como portera, era una delantera increíble. No se hace raro, le das normalidad, son etapas, y estoy muy contenta de que esté aquí. Se acerca el final del 2026. ¿Qué le pide al 2027? Salud, creo que es lo más importante para una futbolista; que me respeten las lesiones. Yo creo que si tengo eso, lo demás llegará solo. ¿Y ganar otra vez un Mundial? Sí, ojalá que sí, eso es un sueño que siempre está ahí.

articles.title: 🥐 From 2030 World Cup final to Haaland bombshell: Friday's top 5️⃣
articles.summary: Friday, November 27, 2026 kicks off with football's agenda heating up amid boardroom battles, transfer rumours and European setbacks. The political debate ov...
articles.body:
Friday, November 27, 2026 kicks off with football's agenda heating up amid boardroom battles, transfer rumours and European setbacks. The political debate over the venue for the 2030 World Cup final, a bombshell prediction from England about the futures of Vinicius and Haaland, and a nightmare night for Spanish clubs in Europe make up the day's five key stories.

Political tug-of-war over the 2030 World Cup final...

The 2030 World Cup made its way into last night's four-way election debate. Prime Minister and PSOE candidate Pedro Sánchez called for Spain to host the final, saying that despite being an Atlético fan, he understands that it should be played at the Santiago Bernabéu.

...And Rufián wants his moment in the spotlight today (as usual)

However, Gabriel Rufián (ERC) poured cold water on the idea in an interview with AS: he is convinced the final will not be held in Spain because Gianni Infantino will need the votes of influential countries such as Morocco to secure re-election.

Haaland in white and goodbye to Vinicius?

A transfer bombshell has emerged from England. Former player Gary Neville predicted on The Overlap podcast that Real Madrid will sell Vinicius Jr. to sign Erling Haaland within the next year and a half. His theory is that the Norwegian would arrive as an out-and-out No. 9 to form a dream attack alongside Kylian Mbappé, who would move to his natural position on the left wing.

A nightmare night in Europe for Spanish football

It was a European matchday to forget in the Europa League and Conference League. Real Sociedad surrendered their lead to lose to Crystal Palace (2-1), and Celta suffered the same fate against Bournemouth (1-2). Getafe, meanwhile, slipped up in Georgia against FC Iberia (1-0). The overall picture is bleak: there are currently no Spanish teams in the top 24 of either competition.

The only joy came from the Under-17 World Cup. Spain rounded off the group stage in convincing fashion yesterday with a 2-0 win over Morocco. Ebrima Tunkara (FC Barcelona) and Guillermo Trujillano (Atlético de Madrid) scored the goals in a victory that keeps the youngsters' dreams firmly alive.

articles.title: PSG make fresh enquiry for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez amid injury crisis as Arsenal stay on alert
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain have reportedly made a fresh enquiry for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez as they deal with a severe attacking injury crisis ahead...
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain have reportedly made a fresh enquiry for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez as they deal with a severe attacking injury crisis ahead of January. The European champions' renewed interest has also kept long-term admirers Arsenal on alert, though both the Spanish club and the player's camp have shut down any mid-season exit.

According to TEAMtalk , PSG are assessing the forward market after Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both suffered season-ending injuries. While the French giants already have several wingers on their shortlist, they have also checked on Alvarez's availability. However, Atletico have no intention of selling mid-season, and the striker's representatives insist a January move is not under consideration.

Simeone backs resurgent Argentine striker

Sources in Madrid stress that Alvarez is not pushing for a winter exit, especially as he is enjoying a strong resurgence after being left out of Diego Simeone's plans earlier in the campaign. The 25-year-old has rediscovered his best form across his last 10 appearances for club and country, contributing six goals and four assists, including a strike in Wednesday's Champions League win over Viking .

Publicly reaffirming his faith in the forward after that victory, Simeone said: "I'm happy with him. I love him as a person, and I'm going to back him as a footballer. There's no play that doesn't go through him and isn't important. I have no doubts. To get where we want to be, we need the best Julian Alvarez."

Both PSG and Arsenal previously tracked the Argentina international during the summer when a transfer saga involving Barcelona developed. Although Alvarez was keen to explore a switch to Catalunya, Atletico stood firm and blocked his departure, prompting the former Manchester City forward to return to the Spanish capital and apologise.

The report states that Arsenal remain aware of PSG's renewed approach and continue to view Alvarez as a player who could significantly upgrade Mikel Arteta's attack. The Gunners' hopes of a mid-season deal had even grown last month amid claims that Martin Zubimendi could be offered in a swap deal .

With Simeone determined to get the best out of Alvarez, a January transfer is firmly off the table for both PSG and Arsenal. The French champions will likely have to turn to the wingers on their shortlist to cover for Doue and Kvaratskhelia this winter. Nevertheless, another major transfer battle for the Argentine is expected to erupt at the end of the season.

articles.title: 'I disagree with Carra!' - Xabi Alonso hits back at Jamie Carragher after Liverpool legend blasts Chelsea duo as a 'massive problem'
articles.summary: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has issued a firm rebuttal to criticism from his former Liverpool teammate Jamie Carragher regarding the Blues' defensive stabili...
articles.body:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has issued a firm rebuttal to criticism from his former Liverpool teammate Jamie Carragher regarding the Blues' defensive stability. The pundit had suggested that the west London club face a significant crisis at the back that could derail their Champions League ambitions.

Alonso stands by Colwill and Fofana after Leeds humbling

Following a 4-1 home defeat by Leeds last weekend, Chelsea's defensive record came under intense scrutiny. The loss left the Blues eighth in the Premier League with just one win in five matches across all competitions.

Only Coventry and bottom-two sides Crystal Palace and Manchester United have conceded more than Chelsea's 20 goals in 11 league games. With Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana pairing up against Leeds, Sky Sports pundit Carragher urged January reinforcements.

Carragher questions leadership before Alonso fires back

On Monday Night Football , Carragher questioned the duo's physicality and leadership. "Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," he said. "As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there."

Put to him at Thursday's press conference, Alonso defended his players. "I must disagree. I disagree with Carra," he said. "For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good [against Leeds]. But I think I've seen them (Colwill and Fofana) play well and I've seen them show good levels.

"This is the goal and the challenge - to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent."

Attacking flair undermined by defensive fragility

While Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, and Joao Pedro have powered an exciting attack when fit, defensive lapses continue to stall Chelsea's progress. Alonso accepted blame and stressed his squad need time to adapt.

"There are no excuses not to do better," he said. "We are in the process. Taking steps, taking a step forward but until it is totally in the DNA of the team it takes time. I take the whole responsibility of the team and how they perform. We need to show [improvement against Nottingham Forest], not just talk. Talk is cheap. It's about performing on the pitch.

"We want to be back on that more solid feeling that we had. This was hopefully one-[off], and we don't want to repeat it."

Injuries force Alonso's hand for Forest clash

Friday's clash with Forest offers an immediate test, though injuries leave Alonso little room to rotate. Defenders Reece James, Maxence Lacroix, and Jorrel Hato remain out, meaning Colwill and Fofana are likely to keep their places.

Star striker Joao Pedro also remains sidelined in another setback, but midfielder Moises Caicedo has been passed fit to play.

articles.title: Now at least 7 Brighton players set to miss Newcastle United match after latest blow
articles.summary: Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been hit by yet another injury ahead of facing Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier Leag...
articles.body:
Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been hit by yet another injury ahead of facing Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier League .

The Seagulls were in action on Thursday night before lining up against Newcastle United .

The south coast club playing Universitatea Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Fabian Hurzeler needs as many players available as possible as he looks to compete in both Europe and the domestic competitions.

In the 39th minute of last night's match, the Brighton boss saw Matt O'Riley on the end of a really poor challenge from Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu, who was then sent off after VAR review.

O'Riley tried to carry on but had to be replaced at the break and Fabian Hurzeler admitted after the match that it doesn't look good for the Denmark international. The Brighton Head Coach revealing that the player's ankle was very swollen.

This looks set to make it at least seven Brighton players ruled out of the Newcastle United match.

Malik Yalcouye was the latest long-term injury to hit the Seagulls ahead of last night's game, whilst also ruled out are Kaoru Mitoma (knee), Stefanos Tzimas (thigh), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh).

Making it at least now seven Brighton players set to miss the Newcastle United match, as Joao Costinha is suspended after having been sent off during the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last weekend.

Other than the new injury for Fabian Hurzeler to deal with though, there wasn't a lot of encouragement for Newcastle United from Brighton having this extra fixture to deal with ahead of Sunday.

The weak Conference League is very different to the demands of the Champions League.

Fabian Hurzeler was able to make eight changes and the Seagulls still cruised to victory against this weak Romanian opposition.

Only Maxim De Cuyper, Pascal Gross and Chema Andres stayed in the team from their Premier League defeat against Hull City and once they took the lead inside three minutes the result was never in doubt.

They were two up after 33 minutes and then when the opposition went down to ten men it was easy street for the Brighton players. The final score ended up 4-0 but if they had really needed a bigger scoreline, who knows what it could have been if they had went all out in this game, rather than having both eyes on Newcastle United less than 72 hours later.

articles.title: Hull City should be in League One this season according to Expected Goals - so how do the Tigers keep winning in the Premier League?
articles.summary: Hull City are sitting comfortably in the middle of the Premier League table - when the Expected Goals underlying data says they should be two divisions below; watch Crystal Palace vs Hull live on Sky Sports this Sunday from 1pm, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
These are all the right ingredients for survival. But the underlying data says otherwise.

If Expected Goals (xG) decided football matches - yes, yes, we know they don't - then Hull would be bottom of the Premier League, with a similar record to the actual bottom club Crystal Palace, who they play live on Sky Sports this Sunday.

The reason? Hull have only won one game this season on xG since their promotion to the top flight.On its own, this underlying data should be taken with a pinch of salt. xG numbers in a match require context.

For example, a team that loses a game can often end up having a higher xG than the opponent, as they were chasing the game and attacking for longer periods.

The same xG table also has Chelsea in 14th place at the moment. Bournemouth should be third and Nottingham Forest should be sixth. After 11 games, there is a lot of differentiation between the Expected Table and the actual table across the board.

But this isn't a new phenomenon when it comes to Hull. The fascinating thing about the Tigers is that this has been happening for 18 months.

The same xG data says Hull should also be playing in League One this season. That's because last term, they should have finished second-bottom of the Championship after 46 games, according to xG. Instead, they were promoted to the Premier League via the play-offs.

As Aston Villa showed last season , you can get away with overperforming this way for some time but things eventually regress to the mean. To do this over a long period of time is extraordinary.

So why are Hull where they are? Style has something to do with it.

Set up in a 5-4-1 formation, Hull have the lowest possession in the Premier League this season by an absolute country mile. The same applies for the number of shots they have and how high they start pressing up the pitch.

"It is not about possession, it is what you do with it," said manager Sergej Jakirovic told Sky Sports in an interview last month . Hull are comfortable in a low block, which ultimately leads to losing the 'stats side' of games.

So how do Hull actually win games? As their manager says, in the little time Hull get hold of the ball, they use it to good effect - the Tigers move the ball up the pitch quicker than any other team.

There is also an efficiency in attack. In the Championship last season, Hull had two of the most clinical forwards in Ollie McBurnie and Joe Gelhardt . They were given few opportunities, but when they got them, they took them.

The same culture applies here. "No matter who is the opponent, we will have our chances," added Jakirovic.

The aim of the game is not only to progress the ball as quickly as possible, but also choosing the right battles. That can be seen in Hull's pressing.

Hull barely press - they have the lowest number of high turnovers in the Premier League this season. However, they have the second-most goals from high turnovers this season and rank fourth for high pressures that end up in a shot. It's a selective, patient press.

Take their recent draw with Brentford as an example. Their only chance of the first half came from Hull pressing out-of-position midfielder Aaron Hickey to win a penalty which they scored from. Then they relied on the defence to hold out for a result. They conceded late, but got what many would say is a good point.

But this game plan of little possession and reliance on taking advantage of the few attacks that come their way is risky. You need a lot of luck to go your way, and Hull have had their fair share of that.

In the Championship last season , Hull had the most let-offs out of any second-tier team in terms of big chances missed by their opponents. A similar theme has continued in the Premier League.

In Hull's first two home games of the season, Man Utd and Aston Villa should have scored around two goals each, according to xG. Neither of those teams found the net, as the Tigers picked up four points instead.

But it is not just luck. In their most recent home game against Brighton, the performance of Konstantinos Tzolakis caught the eye, which confirms skills matters as well.

The Greek goalkeeper - or 'Greek God' as many Hull fans were claiming last weekend - has the best save record out of any Premier League goalkeeper this season. He alone has prevented nearly 2.0 worth of xG going in.

Without him, and without the game plan from their experienced manager, Hull would be closer to the bottom of the table. Instead, they go to the Premier League's basement club knowing they can still get a result.

articles.title: Jonas Urbig is ready to succeed Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer per Sven Ulreich
articles.summary: The veteran listed two key qualities to excel as the goalkeeper of FC Bayern.
articles.body:
Sven Ulreich has served Bayern Munich as the backup goalkeeper for over a decade. Being the deputy to one of the greatest goalkeepers in Manuel Neuer, Ulreich was called into action only during injury spells for the GOATkeeper. Ulreich opined that Urbig possesses the consistency and sheer skill that saw Neuer rule the sport.

In a recent interview with Kicker's Frank Linkesch and Mario Krischel , Sven Ulreich was asked what he thought of Jonas Urbig becoming Bayern's primary goalkeeper after Neuer eventually hangs up his boots.

"He has everything it takes and has already put in some excellent performances for Bayern. He has superb goalkeeping technique, quick reflexes, and is very good with the ball at his feet. He simply has tremendous quality," answered Ulreich (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Urbig undoubtedly has the talent to reach the very top, as seen in his performances during his days at 1. FC Köln and since donning the Bayern shirt. Most recently, he made an incredible double save against his old club on matchday 10. Köln took the game to the Bavarians and managed to create lethal chances with a rapid counterattack strategy. Urbig really saved the game for Bayern and was vital in preventing a loss.

But the wily Ulreich, who has held onto the backup keeper spot for what feels like forever at Bayern, knows what it takes to remain at the top once you get there. "I believe he is already very mentally mature for his young age. Ultimately, that's what makes the difference at Bayern: how do you handle the mental demands when you become the number one and have to deliver consistently, week after week? I have confidence in Jonas because he strikes me as a very level-headed person, always performs at a high level in training, and has already played very well," added Ulreich as he heaped praise on the 23-year-old.

Neuer's latest injury has given Urbig uninterrupted game time to further hone his craft and prepare to take up the number one spot soon.

articles.title: Adama Traore backs Hansi Flick ahead of Barcelona reunion: ‘The team is in very good shape’
articles.summary: Adama Traore has praised Barcelona’s progress under Hansi Flick ahead of Deportivo de A Coruna’s meeting with his former club, while making clear that he hop...
articles.body:
Adama Traore has praised Barcelona's progress under Hansi Flick ahead of Deportivo de A Coruna's meeting with his former club, while making clear that he hopes the Catalans' impressive form does not continue this weekend.

The Deportivo winger, who is still a Barcelona supporter, believes Flick has successfully brought the best out of the squad.

In an interview published by FutbolFantasy , Traore reflected on Barcelona's improvement and discussed how Deportivo intend to approach the challenge of facing one of La Liga's strongest teams. His comments carry added significance given his history with the club.

Traore's Barcelona connection goes back to La Masia

It must be remembered that Traore joined Barcelona's youth academy at the age of eight and progressed to the first team before leaving for Aston Villa in 2015.

He later played for Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers before returning to Camp Nou on loan in January 2022.

The winger made 17 appearances during his second spell, but Barcelona chose not to activate the option to make the transfer permanent. He subsequently returned to Wolves before continuing his career in England.

Adama Traore came through Barcelona's youth system. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

Now playing for Deportivo, Traore will face the club where his professional journey began, with his personal affection for Barcelona still evident.

Traore believes Flick has transformed Barcelona

During the interview, the 30-year-old winger was asked to assess Barcelona's current form, to which Traore said

"I'm a Barcelona fan, so I think the team is in very good shape. When I was there, the club went through a much tougher period.

"But Barcelona are now heading in the right direction. I think Hansi Flick has succeeded, and continues to succeed, in getting the best out of the players

"I hope they carry on like this, though not in this week's match."

How will Deportivo prepare to challenge Barcelona?

Adama Traore will face Barcelona this weekend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Barcelona's form is a difficult challenge for Deportivo, but Traore insists his team will follow their manager's instructions and compete for victory.

"The manager will have the answer. We'll try to follow his instructions and the tactical plan he sets out. And then, we'll give it our all on the pitch to win."

Despite being away from the Barcelona setup for a very long time now, there are still many players in the current roster with whom he shared the dressing room.

"I've shared a dressing room with many of them: Gavi, Pedri, Frenkie de Jong, Eric García, Alejandro Balde.

"There are some who aren't there anymore, who've moved on. Their talent is incredible, and it's a real pleasure to be around them," he concluded.

articles.title: Holanda ya conoce a Mario Domínguez: "No hay mejor liberación que el gol"
articles.standfirst: El delantero valencianista, cedido en el Excelsior, estrenó su cuenta en la Eredivisie ante el Feyenoord, en un derbi que devolvió la sonrisa a su equipo y a él mismo
articles.summary: El delantero valencianista, cedido en el Excelsior, estrenó su cuenta en la Eredivisie ante el Feyenoord, en un derbi que devolvió la sonrisa a su equipo y a él mismo
articles.body: Mario Domínguez (Granada, 2004) tiene el gol en la sangre. Lo ha demostrado siempre. Primero en la cantera del Valencia y lo acaba de presentar también en Países Bajos, en un escenario que difícilmente podría haber elegido mejor para darse a conocer. De Kuip, el templo del Feyenoord, uno de los gigantes del fútbol neerlandés y habitual de la Champions League. Allí, en el derbi de Rotterdam, estrenó su cuenta en la Eredivisie. Y lo hizo con un triunfo que lleva su firma. No necesitó demasiados adornos. Leyó el espacio entre centrales, atacó la profundidad, trazó el desmarque con la intuición de quien sabe dónde va a caer la pelota y resolvió con una definición sencilla, haciendo fácil lo difícil. El empate del Excelsior, además, llegó en un momento clave: significó el punto de partida de una remontada emocional y competitiva. "El gol ha sido una liberación. Estoy acostumbrado a marcar y no me estaba sintiendo yo. No me entraba la pelota y este fin de semana ha sido un chute de confianza que necesitaba. Ahora toca seguir mirando hacia delante y sumar para ayudar al equipo a ganar", reconoce en declaraciones a MARCA. El Excelsior llegaba a De Kuip con urgencias. No ganaba desde principios de septiembre, acumulaba ocho partidos con apenas dos empates y había encajado golpes difíciles de digerir, como las derrotas ante Heerenveen, Groningen o el contundente 0-9 frente al Twente. El derbi aparecía como una oportunidad, pero también como una prueba de resistencia. El Feyenoord golpeó primero. El Excelsior, sin embargo, encontró la manera de levantarse. El 2-3 final tuvo mucho de supervivencia. Ganar en De Kuip siempre es motivo de orgullo, pero hacerlo cuando llevas semanas buscando respuestas puede cambiar el tono de una temporada. "Estábamos trabajando bien, pero nos estaban faltando los resultados. No hay mejor refuerzo ni mejor manera de recargar energías que ganar un derbi en el campo del Feyenoord", explica. El Excelsior afronta ahora el encuentro de este sábado ante el Telstar, un rival directo, con otra perspectiva. La victoria ha cambiado el ambiente, ha reforzado la confianza y ha devuelto al equipo una recompensa que necesitaba. Y Mario, que ya ha encontrado el gol, comienza a encontrar también su lugar. Un salto de fútbol, de contexto y de vida La aventura neerlandesa representa mucho más que un cambio de camiseta para el delantero granadino. Formado en el Valencia, donde ha desarrollado prácticamente toda su trayectoria, esta es su primera experiencia lejos de su casa futbolística. El salto es considerable: de la Segunda RFEF, donde ha competido las últimas temporadas con el Valencia Mestalla, a la Eredivisie. Del Antonio Puchades y los partidos ante el Alcoyano, el Barbastro o el Reus, a enfrentarse a Ajax, PSV Eindhoven o Feyenoord. Holanda aparecía como un contexto idóneo para continuar su desarrollo. Un fútbol que favorece el talento joven, con espacios, ritmo y una cultura ofensiva que puede ayudar a crecer a los atacantes. El Excelsior no es uno de los grandes dominadores de la competición, pero la elección respondía a una apuesta por la continuidad, la confianza y un entorno en el que Mario pudiera empezar a construir su camino en la élite.. El aterrizaje, no obstante, tuvo sus dificultades. Su pretemporada estuvo condicionada por problemas físicos que le impidieron prepararse como hubiera deseado. A ello se sumaron el idioma, una cultura futbolística diferente, un nuevo vestuario y las exigencias de una competición de mayor nivel. "El principio no ha sido fácil, condicionado también por la pretemporada en Valencia. Me ha costado adaptarme porque el fútbol aquí es diferente, tanto en la idea de juego como en el aspecto físico. Aun así, los compañeros me lo han puesto muy fácil y me he adaptado rápido", admite. Valencia no quiso dejar escapar al goleador Mario llegó a Holanda el pasado verano después de renovar con el Valencia. En Mestalla entendían que no podían dejar escapar a un futbolista que había despertado interés de equipos de Primera División y de otros clubes europeos. El plan inicial pasaba por realizar la pretemporada con el primer equipo y explorar sus posibilidades de encontrar un espacio en la dinámica de la plantilla, pero los problemas físicos condicionaron esa hoja de ruta. La cesión terminó siendo la alternativa para encontrar continuidad y un escenario competitivo que permitiera acelerar su crecimiento. El Excelsior incorporó al atacante en una operación diseñada para proteger el desarrollo del futbolista y los intereses valencianistas. El club neerlandés cuenta con una opción de compra y el Valencia mantiene mecanismos para recuperar al jugador o participar en una futura operación si su progresión confirma las expectativas. No era una apuesta sin fundamentos. José Bordalás ya le había hecho debutar con el Valencia siendo juvenil. En el Mestalla se convirtió en uno de los grandes referentes ofensivos y en el mejor goleador del filial en las últimas temporadas, hasta situarse entre los máximos anotadores del Valencia Mestalla en el siglo XXI. Su progresión tampoco fue lineal. En 2024 sufrió una grave lesión de rodilla que frenó su crecimiento, pero volvió a levantarse. La mejor respuesta llegó sobre el césped: 17 goles en la última temporada en el Antonio Puchades, una cifra que reforzó su candidatura a dar un nuevo paso.

articles.title: PIF Value Newcastle United At £1.5Bn As They Seek Fresh Investment
articles.summary: Seeking a multi-million pound capital injection to fund a world-class stadium and training complex, the Magpies' owners are courting global investors to acce...
articles.body:
Newcastle United could be worth in the region of £1.5 billion, with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) exploring opportunities to bring fresh external investment into the club as they look to finance an ambitious programme of infrastructure development.

The valuation represents a significant increase on the approximately £305 million paid by the Saudi-backed consortium to complete its takeover of Newcastle United in October 2021.

PIF, which currently holds an 84% majority stake in the club, is understood to be exploring the possibility of selling up to 25% through the issuing of new shares, with investment bank JP Morgan appointed to oversee the process and identify potential investors.

The proposed investment would not represent a full or majority sale of Newcastle United. Instead, it would allow the current ownership structure to bring additional financial partners into the club while PIF retains overall control.

According to reports, the money raised would be directed towards major infrastructure projects, with the long-term stadium plans considered a significant priority.

A potential 25% investment based on a £1.5 billion valuation would generate approximately £375 million, providing Newcastle with substantial additional capital to help move forward with their development ambitions.

However, more recent reports have also suggested that the club's valuation could be considerably higher, with figures approaching or exceeding £2 billion being discussed in connection with potential investor interest.

One of the biggest motivations behind the search for additional investment is Newcastle's long-term ambition to deliver a significantly improved stadium.

Chief Executive David Hopkinson has previously made clear that the club are examining their options, including a potential new stadium or a major redevelopment of St James' Park.

A new stadium project could cost in the region of £1.3 billion, although the final financial requirements will depend on the preferred option and the wider development plans.

The possibility of building a new home for Newcastle United on Leazes Park has generated considerable discussion among supporters, particularly given the opportunity to increase capacity, improve matchday facilities and create additional commercial revenue.

The club are also progressing plans for a new £190 million training complex at Woolsington, which is expected to become operational by 2029.

The facility is another major part of the ownership's ambitions to establish Newcastle as a leading force in English and European football.

Bringing in external investment could help spread the financial burden of these developments rather than requiring PIF to fund every project independently.

Despite speculation surrounding the proposed minority investment, reports suggest that PIF remain committed to Newcastle United and do not view the process as the beginning of a full takeover exit.

The Saudi fund currently owns approximately 84% of Newcastle, with the Reuben family holding the remaining 16% following Amanda Staveley's departure from the ownership structure in 2024.

Any new share issue would dilute existing shareholders, but PIF would be expected to retain its majority position and continue overseeing the club's long-term direction.

The development also comes against the backdrop of increasing financial restrictions within the Premier League, with Newcastle having to carefully manage their spending while competing with clubs possessing significantly greater commercial revenues.

Infrastructure investment could therefore prove particularly important, allowing Newcastle to improve their revenue-generating capabilities through increased stadium capacity, hospitality, sponsorship opportunities and wider commercial development.

A significant moment for Newcastle's future

Newcastle United have come a considerable distance since the 2021 takeover, with Champions League qualification on two occasions and the historic Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 helping restore the club's position among English football's leading sides.

However, the next stage of the project is increasingly focused on building the infrastructure required to sustain that progress.

A reported £1.5 billion valuation highlights the significant growth in Newcastle's standing since the takeover, while the interest in attracting fresh investment demonstrates the scale of the ambitions being considered behind the scenes.

For supporters, the most important question is what this could mean for the future of the club.

If PIF successfully attracts the right investment partners, Newcastle could be in a position to accelerate plans for a new stadium, deliver the proposed training complex and establish a stronger financial platform for the years ahead.

No investment agreement has yet been confirmed, and the precise valuation and financial terms remain subject to negotiations.

Nevertheless, the message is becoming increasingly clear: Newcastle United's owners are exploring ways to fund the next major chapter of the club's development, with infrastructure and long-term growth firmly at the centre of their plans.

articles.title: Uruguay international open to leaving Sporting CP for Man Utd in January as Mauricio Pochettino eyes Luke Shaw replacement
articles.summary: Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo is reportedly open to joining Manchester United in January as Mauricio Pochettino searches for a replacement for injury-hit...
articles.body:
Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo is reportedly open to joining Manchester United in January as Mauricio Pochettino searches for a replacement for injury-hit Luke Shaw. Having tracked the Uruguay international for months, Red Devils officials were convinced after watching him closely during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon.

According to Sport Witness , United used Wednesday's trip to Lisbon to assess Araujo up close and left convinced by the 26-year-old. Making his 14th start in 15 appearances this season, the Uruguay international played the full 90 minutes and assisted Luis Suarez's 33rd-minute opener. Mutual appreciation now exists between both parties, with the defender's camp very open to a winter switch to Old Trafford.

United's admiration for Araujo dates back to April, when they were among several Premier League clubs monitoring his progress. Despite finishing the summer without strengthening that position, reports last month linked both United and Arsenal with renewed plans to pursue him. At that stage, a source informed the outlet that there had been "nothing new" since their initial enquiries earlier in the year.

In August, Araujo had quietened transfer speculation by extending his Sporting contract until 2030, securing a top salary alongside an €80 million release clause. However, his commanding display against United has reignited their pursuit, with Pochettino also familiar with his qualities from facing him while in charge of the United States.

The Red Devils' urgent need for reinforcements stems from persistent fitness problems on the left side of defence. Shaw and Harry Amass are the club's only two recognised left-backs, and both have contracts expiring in 2027. Shaw has struggled with numerous injuries throughout his spell in Manchester and has missed the last eight matches with a muscle problem.

In his absence, former manager Michael Carrick mainly deployed Diogo Dalot out of position, while Pochettino opted to start Lisandro Martinez there. The report states that United are expected to enter the winter market for a natural left-back , making the South American an ideal fit for Pochettino's side.

Despite Araujo's €80 million release clause, a fee of €50-60 million would reportedly be enough to prise him away from Sporting in January. However, the same source believes United are unlikely to invest that much on a full-back midway through the season. Whether Pochettino can persuade the Old Trafford hierarchy to sanction the outlay remains to be seen.

articles.title: Greece will 'stretch us' in friendlies - McArdle
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle says Greece were "deliberately picked to stretch us" in two home friendlies, beginning with Friday's first game at I...
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle says Greece were "deliberately picked to stretch us" in two home friendlies, beginning with Friday's first game at Inver Park.

The sides meet again in Larne on Tuesday [16:00] as they begin preparations for their respective Nations League B campaigns in 2027.

Both missed out on qualification for next year's World Cup in Brazil at the play-off stage, with Northern Ireland beaten by Portugal, while Greece were eliminated by England.

This double-header against a Greece side that McArdle feels are "slightly ahead of us" is an ideal way to develop his squad for the challenges ahead.

"They are very pacey, so the counter-attacks will be difficult for us to deal with but we wanted that, wanted to test ourselves that way," McArdle told BBC Sport NI.

"They are a threat in League B and will have the same aspirations as ourselves. They are a nation who are evolving quickly and one that will give us a test in all areas, so they aren't friendlies, more challenge matches and deliberately picked to stretch us."

McArdle believes this camp, which culminates in Northern Ireland's first friendlies in three years, affords them time to reflect and reset before facing Poland, Finland and Belarus next year in the Nations League.

Long-term, there is the 2035 World Cup that Northern Ireland will co-host along with England, Scotland and Wales, and qualification for that is high on the agenda after Belfast was named as a host city.

"That [qualifying] becomes a long-term ambition, but within that there are small moments, smaller journeys and projects," McArdle said.

"We still prepare for Greece in the same detail, but there is more detail towards ourselves in this camp."

While a place at next year's World Cup eluded them, McArdle still holds a sense of "excitement about the underlying potential we have".

The Northern Ireland boss feels consistency is key to their development.

"We've got strong markers and the exciting mix of the squad of those more experienced players and the youthful ambition and energy," he said.

"It gives us a good balance, but at the moment, we're just looking to be a more dominant League B nation and that in turn should give us more opportunities to be successful in play-offs."

articles.title: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk hails 'outstanding' Alexander Isak as Merseyside derby looms
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk has heaped praise on Alexander Isak, describing the Liverpool forward as an "outstanding" talent following his match-winning display in the C...
articles.body:
Virgil van Dijk has heaped praise on Alexander Isak, describing the Liverpool forward as an "outstanding" talent following his match-winning display in the Champions League against Club Brugge. The Swedish international was the star of the show in Belgium, continuing a prolific run of form that has seen him become a vital cog in Andoni Iraola's attacking machine.

Isak hits historic milestone in clinical European triumph

Liverpool maintained their surge in form with a commanding 3-0 Champions League win away to Club Brugge in Belgium. Joint British-record signing Alexander Isak netted twice - capping the night with a clever run and chip over Yann Sommer - alongside a strike from Florian Wirtz.

The double lifted the Sweden international to 10 goals this season, including seven in his past 10 outings. Isak also became only the eighth player in club history to score in six consecutive away games, putting an injury-hit maiden campaign firmly behind him.

Van Dijk applauds Isak's work rate and growing chemistry

Van Dijk praised how the forward's physicality and link-up play elevate the team alongside his finishing.

"Hopefully there are many more goals to come. He's an outstanding striker. On and off the ball he's so important for us. His hold up play was so good, how he carried the ball," the Liverpool captain said. "Sometimes when we had to go long, it was difficult for him to win the first ball but he was always there to fight and make it difficult for the defenders."

The veteran centre-back also credited renewed self-belief and fitness for Isak's resurgence. "It's difficult for me to say [what has changed for Isak] but confidence is massive," he continued. "Staying fit, looking after yourself, knowing what the demands are to be a Liverpool player. Finding your importance in the team helps as well. Alex knows what we need from him and he's delivering that. I think it can only get better from here."

He added that squad cohesion is steadily building: "Everyone has to understand each other's strengths and also sometimes their weaknesses in order to get the best out of each other. The process is going well."

Reds brace for derby backlash despite contrasting form

Following last weekend's win over Manchester United and their European triumph, Liverpool visit Hill Dickinson Stadium as favourites. The Reds have won five and lost just one of their recent cross-city clashes, while Everton saw their progress halted by a chastening 4-0 defeat at Brentford with 10 men.

Despite that contrast, Van Dijk expects a fierce derby response. "We are having a great week [but] I expect fireworks on Sunday, given Everton's result in their last game," he noted. "They are going to come up with a reaction, something comes out of that. You already know that."

Having scored a winner in the 10th minute of stoppage time there in April, the Dutchman anticipates another testing early kick-off. "It will be intense again on Sunday but these are the kind of games you look forward to," he added. "They had a difficult result on Monday and they will want to show a reaction. Like when you play Manchester United, this is a game on its own. It will be tough. It's a very early kick off but we have to be ready."

Chance to cap a pivotal week with four straight wins

Victory in Sunday's first Merseyside derby of the season would seal a third straight win in eight days and a fourth in a row overall for Liverpool. Sustaining the sharp attacking form of Isak and Wirtz will prove crucial as a pivotal stretch of the campaign unfolds. Overcoming a wounded Everton side hungry for revenge would underline the Reds' growing momentum.

articles.title: Louisville vs Kentucky Prediction: The Governor's Cup Means Something More Now
articles.summary: Louisville and Kentucky are both good, with a lot to look forward to. Now the rivalry game means something extra. Here's the CFN preview and prediction.
articles.body:
The Battle of the Bluegrass – or, if you prefer, for the Governor's Cup – is always one of those fun rivalry games between Louisville and Kentucky at or near the end of the season, but it's a true regional battle. Does it really matter all that much on a national scale? Yeah, it's getting stronger thanks to the consistent success of head coach Jeff Brohm at Louisville, and with Will Stein turning Kentucky into a rising power. The Wildcats might have slipped out of the CFP Top 25, but they've been in the mix over the last several weeks. Louisville is currently No. 19, and it might be the best ACC team available in the bowl process.

Louisville has won six straight since losing back-to-back ACC games in late September. The 30-27 loss to Wake Forest was the difference between playing for the ACC Championship and finishing third in the conference.

Kentucky started 7-1 but lost three straight. It's a win a way from this being the program's best season since 2021.

Louisville won 41-0 last year, but Kentucky is 5-2 in the last seven meetings.

Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN2 Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections

Kentucky has stopped scoring. The offense wasn't horrible in last week's 28-14 loss to Missouri, and the passing attack wasn't awful in the loss to Tennessee, but the ground attack was stuffed by Florida, and the three turnovers against both the Vols and Tigers were a killer. Louisville's offense has been solid over the second half of the season, but it's the attacking defense that's taking over games. The Cardinals have forced 13 turnovers over their six-game winning run.

The Wildcats have to start taking the ball away again. That was part of the puzzle when the team was rolling, with 18 takeaways in the first eight games. There has been just one over this last three-game losing streak. Start forcing mistakes again, and the overall production will follow. UK quarterback Kenny Minchey has to crank up the big plays. All three Louisville losses came when the defense got hit by a slew of deep shots – Wake Forest, NC State, and Ole Miss all averaged over nine yards per throw.

Louisville vs Kentucky Prediction, Betting Lines

Kentucky has the talent, coaching, and experience to pull this off after losing the last two years by a combined score of 82-14. It's far better this season, but Louisville is too sharp, with too good a running game to be slowed to a crawl. It'll be a good, entertaining game, but Kentucky won't be able to score enough – it's 0-4 when scoring fewer than 21. It takes 30 to beat the Cardinals as the rivalry enters a new phase.

articles.title: Familiar faces and surprise chances as Ireland face Wallabies
articles.summary: Ireland aim to round out a successful November with victory over Australia in what Andy Farrell is treating as a dry-run before next year's World Cup.
articles.body:
Discussion about how Ireland head coach Andy Farrell would approach Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia was ended emphatically by the team announcement on Wednesday.

While Farrell would have been excused for fielding a rotated side in the wake of last week's bruising victory over world champions South Africa , he instead opted for continuity and is challenging his first-choice line-up to produce another chest-thumping 80-minute display against the Wallabies.

Farrell has made two changes from the side that started Saturday's 20-17 success over the Springboks in Dublin, both of which are enforced.

Jacob Stockdale replaces the ill Mack Hansen on the left wing while in-form back row Nick Timoney is restored at number eight in place of the banned Dan Sheehan.

While Ireland cannot win the inaugural Nations Championship, Farrell has emphasised the importance of Friday in the context of the team's journey to next year's World Cup.

A win over Australia would be four wins in as many weekends. Do that down under next year and Ireland will find themselves in another World Cup quarter-final.

The six-day turnaround between last week's win over South Africa and Friday's contest with Australia serves as useful preparation for next year's tournament, where Ireland will have six days between their pool games against Portugal and Scotland and potentially a quarter and semi-final, should they reach that stage.

With no six-day turnarounds in the 2027 Six Nations, Farrell is keen to test his side within those parameters before they return to their provinces for a busy festive schedule.

While the World Cup unavoidably edges into view, Ireland's immediate priority is to close out a largely positive 2026 on a winning note.

Sobering defeats by France and New Zealand cast doubts over the squad's trajectory, but last week's narrow win over South Africa served as a reminder that Farrell's side can still mix it with the world's best.

And while slaying the Springboks may have restored hope among fans, senior squad figures have carefully tempered expectations as they attempt to round out the year with a 10th win from 12 Tests.

"If you're winning games by the skin of your teeth and not performing well you don't really gain that belief, but when you're playing well and then start winning well the belief comes and that's something that we certainly gained before the 2023 World Cup," said Tadhg Beirne, who will captain Ireland against Australia in Sheehan's absence.

"But we're building that and we're often talking about that in terms of creating that belief, creating that identity that we want to see of ourselves, but again we're nowhere near where we need to be if we want to be competing to win a World Cup next year.

"I think there's so much more growth but we have to keep delivering in these big games for everyone to feel it and I know how it feels back in 2023 going into that World Cup.

"I think everyone in that squad felt it and I think we're certainly on the way there and if we can keep performing the way we've been performing but getting better we'll certainly be there by next year."

Friday night is a big opportunity for Stockdale, who was not involved in the wins over Argentina, Fiji and South Africa.

Nearly nine years removed from his star-making performances for Joe Schmidt's Ireland in the 2018 Grand Slam campaign, the 30-year-old Ulster wing is no longer a nailed-on starter.

But having been picked ahead of Tommy O'Brien - who scored two tries in the win over Fiji - Stockdale must seize an opportunity to impress on what will be his first run-out at Twickenham since a try-scoring cameo off the bench in a behind-closed-doors Autumn Nations Cup defeat by England in November 2020.

Stockdale needn't look far for inspiration. Seven of his Ulster team-mates are in the matchday 23. Two of them - Stuart McCloskey and Timoney - have featured in all 12 Tests this year (alongside Beirne), while jet-heeled right winger Robert Baloucoune is enjoying his best run as an international after a couple of tries against South Africa last week.

In January 2016, Stockdale made his Ulster debut under the province's then director of rugby Les Kiss, the man now leading the Wallabies.

The 61-year-old replaced Schmidt following the July leg of the Nations Championship, and while scrutiny on the Queenslander intensified following defeats by England and Scotland, last week's 29-26 victory over Wales has boosted the Wallaby morale as they attempt to snap a six-game losing streak against the Irish.

Kiss, who was Ireland's defence coach during the historic 2009 Grand Slam triumph, has turned heads with his own selection in the number 11 jersey, with former Northampton Saints winger James Ramm earning his Test debut at the age of 28.

Kurtley Beale - who started Australia's last victory over Ireland in June 2018 - is an eye-catching addition to the bench as the 37-year-old closes in on a first Test cap in five years.

With Kalani Thomas earning a first start at scrum-half and a new back-row combination in Tom Hooper, Carlo Tizzano and Rob Valetini, it is an intriguing Wallabies line-up.

But if Ireland can replicate the intensity and edge they showed against South Africa, they may pass Farrell's World Cup rehearsal and ensure they approach the tantalising possibilities of 2027 in buoyant form.

Ireland: Keenan; Baloucoune, Henshaw, McCloskey, Stockdale; Prendergast, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong, McCarthy, Beirne (capt), Baird, Van der Flier, Timoney.

Replacements: Stewart, O'Toole, Clarkson, Ryan, McNabney, Doak, Frawley, Aki.

Australia: Wright; Jorgensen, Suaalii, Ikitau, Ramm; Gordon, Thomas; Kailea, Paenga-Amosa, Alaalatoa (co-capt), Canham, Williams, Hooper, Tizzano, Valetini.

Replacements: Nasser, Bell, Tupou, Shaw, Wilson (co-capt), McReight, Wilson, Beale.
